title.zh: 卷三百六十八 列傳第一百二十七 王德 王彥 魏勝 張憲 楊再興 牛皋 胡閎休
title.en: Volume 368 Biographies 127: Wang De, Wang Yan, Wei Sheng, Zhang Xian, Yang Zaixing, Niu Gao, Hu Hongxiu
title.raw: 卷三百六十八 列傳第一百二十七 王德 王彥 魏勝 張憲 楊再興 牛皋 胡閎休 Volume 368 Biographies 127: Wang De, Wang Yan, Wei Sheng, Zhang Xian, Yang Zaixing, Niu Gao, Hu Hongxiu

sentences.zh: 王德 王彥 魏勝 張憲 楊再興 牛皋 胡閎休

translations.literal: Wang De, Wang Yan, Wei Sheng, Zhang Xian, Yang Zaixing, Niu Gao, Hu Hongxiu
translations.idiomatic: Wang De, Wang Yan, Wei Sheng, Zhang Xian, Yang Zaixing, Niu Gao, and Hu Hongxiu

sentences.zh: 王德，字子華，通遠軍熟羊砦人。

translations.literal: Wang De, courtesy name Zihua, was a man of Shuyang Stockade in Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De, styled Zihua, came from Shuyang Stockade in the Tongyuan Army district.

sentences.zh: 以武勇應募，隸熙帥姚古。

translations.literal: He enlisted for his martial valor and was attached to Yao Gu, commander of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered on account of his fighting prowess and served under Yao Gu, military commissioner of the Xi circuit.

sentences.zh: 會金人入侵，古軍懷、澤間，遣德諜之，斬一酋而還。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded, Gu stationed his army between Huai and Ze, sent De to spy, beheaded one chieftain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded, Yao Gu held his forces between Huai and Ze and sent Wang De to scout; Wang De cut down an enemy leader and came back.

sentences.zh: 補進武校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Military School Captain.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Senior Military Academy Officer.

sentences.zh: 古曰：「能復往乎？

translations.literal: Gu said, "Can you go again?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gu asked, "Could you go back again?"

sentences.zh: 」德從十六騎徑入隆德府治，執偽守姚太師，左右驚擾，德手殺數十百人，眾愕眙莫取前。

translations.literal: De took sixteen horsemen straight into the seat of Longde Prefecture, seized the false prefect Yao the Grand Master; those around were alarmed and thrown into disorder; De personally killed scores of men; the crowd stared in dismay and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: With only sixteen riders Wang De rode straight into the Longde prefectural seat, seized the puppet prefect Yao Taishi, and threw his attendants into panic. He killed dozens of men with his own hand; the rest stood dumbfounded and did not dare come forward.

sentences.zh: 古械姚獻於朝，欽宗問狀，姚曰：「臣就縛時，止見一夜叉耳。

translations.literal: Gu sent Yao in fetters to the court; Emperor Qinzong questioned him; Yao said, "When I was taken, I saw only a yaksha."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gu had Yao brought to court in chains. When Emperor Qinzong questioned him, Yao said, "When they seized me, I saw nothing but a yaksha demon."

sentences.zh: 」時遂呼德為「王夜叉」。

translations.literal: At the time people therefore called De "Wang the Yaksha."
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wang De was known as "Wang the Yaksha."

sentences.zh: 三年春，遷前軍統領，屯天長。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was transferred to commander of the vanguard and encamped at Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was made commander of the vanguard and stationed at Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 金人攻揚州，西軍多潰，德趨宣化。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked Yangzhou; many western armies collapsed; De hastened to Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Yangzhou and many western armies broke, Wang De rushed to Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 會叛將張昱、張彥圍和州，太守張績求援於德，德兵傅城下，賊不意其至，大潰。

translations.literal: When the rebel generals Zhang Yu and Zhang Yan besieged He Prefecture, the prefect Zhang Ji sought aid from De; De's troops pressed against the city wall; the bandits did not expect his arrival and were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel generals Zhang Yu and Zhang Yan besieged Hezhou, Prefect Zhang Ji asked Wang De for help. Wang De pressed his troops against the walls; the rebels did not expect him and fled in complete disorder.

sentences.zh: 遲明接戰，斬昱，俘其兵騎萬數，濟自採石。

translations.literal: At dawn he joined battle, beheaded Yu, captured his soldiers and horsemen by the tens of thousands, and crossed from Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he gave battle, killed Zhang Yu, took tens of thousands of his soldiers and horses prisoner, and crossed the river from Caishi.

sentences.zh: 光世方謀討苗、劉之逆，迎至建康，謂德曰：「江都之擾，諸軍不竄則盜。

translations.literal: Guangshi was then planning to suppress the rebellion of Miao and Liu; he welcomed De to Jiankang and said to him, "In the turmoil at Jiangdu, if the armies do not flee they become bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi was then planning to put down the rebellion of Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan. He welcomed Wang De to Jiankang and told him, "In the upheaval at Jiangdu, any army that does not scatter will turn to plunder."

sentences.zh: 公可仗義夜涉大江，徇國急變。

translations.literal: You may act on righteousness, cross the great river by night, and answer the state's urgent crisis.
translations.idiomatic: You can act in the name of duty, cross the Yangtze by night, and answer the empire's urgent need.

sentences.zh: 」遂以軍屬光世。

translations.literal: His army was then placed under Guangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De then placed his army under Liu Guangshi's command.

sentences.zh: 會苗、劉走閩中，詔德追擊，隸韓世忠。

translations.literal: When Miao and Liu fled into Min, an edict ordered De to pursue; he was attached to Han Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao and Liu fled into Fujian, the court ordered Wang De to pursue them, and he was placed under Han Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 德欲自致功名，而世忠必欲德為之使，遣親將陳彥章邀德於信州。

translations.literal: De wished to win merit on his own, but Shizhong insisted that De serve him; he sent his close general Chen Yanzhang to intercept De at Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De wanted to win glory on his own account, but Han Shizhong was determined to have him serve under him and sent his trusted general Chen Yanzhang to waylay Wang De at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥章拔佩刀擊德，德殺彥章，屍諸市。

translations.literal: Yanzhang drew his sword and struck at De; De killed Yanzhang and exposed his corpse in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang drew his sword and attacked Wang De; Wang De killed him and displayed his body in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 德至浦城，斬苗瑀，擒馬柔吉送行在。

translations.literal: De reached Pucheng, beheaded Miao Yu, seized Ma Rouji, and sent him to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: At Pucheng Wang De killed Miao Yu, captured Ma Rouji, and sent him to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 世忠訟其擅殺，下臺獄，侍御史趙鼎按德當死，帝命特原之，編管郴州。

translations.literal: Shizhong sued him for unauthorized killing; he was sent to the censorial prison; the attendant censor Zhao Ding judged De deserving of death; the emperor ordered special pardon and registered banishment at Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong charged him with murder; he was thrown into prison. Attendant Censor Zhao Ding ruled that Wang De deserved death, but the emperor specially pardoned him and banished him to Chenzhou under registration.

sentences.zh: 時光世屯九江，得楊惟忠所失空頭黃敕，即以便宜復德前軍統制，遣平信州妖賊王念經。

translations.literal: At the time Guangshi was stationed at Jiujiang; he obtained the blank imperial yellow patent lost by Yang Weizhong and, on his own authority, restored De as commander of the vanguard and sent him to pacify the sorcerer-rebel Wang Nianjing of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi was then at Jiujiang. He recovered the blank imperial patent Yang Weizhong had lost and, acting on his own authority, restored Wang De as vanguard commander and sent him to suppress the sorcerer-rebel Wang Nianjing in Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 行次饒州，會賊劉文舜圍城，德引兵赴之，文舜請降。

translations.literal: On the march at Rao Prefecture he encountered the bandit Liu Wenshun besieging the city; De led troops to relieve it; Wenshun asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the march at Raozhou he found the rebel Liu Wenshun besieging the city. Wang De marched to the rescue; Wenshun offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 德納而誅之，自餘不戮一人。

translations.literal: De accepted the surrender and then executed him; beyond that he killed no one.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De accepted the surrender and then executed him, but put no one else to death.

sentences.zh: 謂諸校曰：「念經聞吾宿留，必不為備。

translations.literal: He told the officers, "When Nianjing hears that I am lingering here, he will certainly not be on guard."
translations.idiomatic: He told his officers, "When Nianjing hears that we are stopping here, he will surely let his guard down."

sentences.zh: 」倍道而趨，一鼓擒之，獻俘於朝。

translations.literal: He marched by double stages, captured him in one assault, and presented the captive to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the pace, took Nianjing at the first blow, and sent the prisoner to court.

sentences.zh: 詔還舊秩，加武顯大夫、榮州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict restored his former rank and added Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and prefect of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his former rank and promoted him to Grand Master of Martial Brilliance and prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，光世鎮京口，以德為都統制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Guangshi was posted at Jingkou and made De overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Liu Guangshi was stationed at Jingkou and appointed Wang De overall commander.

sentences.zh: 金兵復南，光世將退保丹陽，德請以死捍江，諸將恃以自強。

translations.literal: The Jin army came south again; Guangshi was about to withdraw and hold Danyang; De asked to defend the river at the cost of his life; the generals relied on him and took heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies marched south again, Liu Guangshi was ready to fall back on Danyang. Wang De asked to defend the Yangtze even at the cost of his life, and the other generals took courage from him.

sentences.zh: 分軍扼險，渡江襲金人，收真、揚數郡。

translations.literal: He divided his army to hold the passes, crossed the river to strike the Jurchens, and recovered several prefectures in Zhen and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He split his forces to hold the defiles, crossed the river to strike the Jin, and recovered several prefectures around Zhen and Yang.

sentences.zh: 既而又遇敵於揚州北，有被重鎧突陣者，德馳叱之；

translations.literal: Later he met the enemy again north of Yangzhou; one man in heavy armor charged the line; De galloped up and shouted at him;
translations.idiomatic: Later he met the enemy again north of Yangzhou. A man in heavy armor charged the line, and Wang De galloped up and shouted him down;

sentences.zh: 重鎧者直前刺德，德揮刀迎之，即墮馬。

translations.literal: the armored man thrust straight at De; De swung his blade to meet him, and the man fell from his horse at once.
translations.idiomatic: the armored man thrust straight at Wang De; Wang De swung his blade to meet him, and the man fell from his horse at once.

sentences.zh: 眾褫駭，因麾騎乘之，所殺萬計。

translations.literal: The host was stricken with fear; he then ordered the cavalry to press them; those killed were counted by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ranks were shaken with fear. He then ordered his cavalry to press the attack and killed men by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 三年，光世宣撫江、淮，當移屯建康，命韓世忠代之。

translations.literal: In the third year Guangshi was commissioner to pacify Jiang and Huai; he was to move his camp to Jiankang; Han Shizhong was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Guangshi was pacification commissioner for the Jiang and Huai region and was to move his headquarters to Jiankang; Han Shizhong was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 德從數十騎自京口逆世忠，度將及麾下，徒步立道左，抗言曰：「擅殺陳彥章，王德迎馬頭請死。

translations.literal: De took several dozen horsemen from Jingkou to meet Shizhong; when he judged that Shizhong was about to reach his retinue, he dismounted, stood on the left of the road, and spoke boldly: "For killing Chen Yanzhang on my own authority, Wang De meets your horse's head and asks for death."
translations.idiomatic: Wang De took several dozen riders from Jingkou to meet Han Shizhong. When he judged that Shizhong was nearly upon him, he dismounted, stood by the roadside, and said plainly, "For killing Chen Yanzhang on my own authority, Wang De meets you at your horse's head and asks for death."

sentences.zh: 」世忠下馬握其手曰：「知公好漢，鄉來纖介不足置懷。

translations.literal: Shizhong dismounted, took his hand, and said, "I know you are a true man; the trifling matter of before is not worth bearing in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong dismounted, took his hand, and said, "I know you are a true fighting man. That little affair before is not worth bearing a grudge over."

sentences.zh: 」乃設酒盡歡而別。

translations.literal: He then set out wine; they drank their fill and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They then shared wine, made merry, and parted.

sentences.zh: 是冬，知鞏州、熙河蘭廓路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: That winter he was made military intendant of Gong Prefecture and of the Xihe, Lan, and Kuo circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made military intendant of Gongzhou and of the Xihe-Lan-Kuo circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年春，知蘭州，徙屯池陽及當塗，為行營左護軍前軍統制。

translations.literal: The next spring he was made prefect of Lan Prefecture, moved his camp to Chiyang and Dangtu, and became commander of the vanguard of the Left Guard Army of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he was made prefect of Lanzhou, shifted his camp to Chiyang and Dangtu, and became commander of the vanguard of the Left Guard Army in the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 金兵掠江北，破滁州。

translations.literal: The Jin army raided north of the river and took Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces raided the north bank of the Yangtze and captured Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 德越江襲奪之，追至桑根，擒女真萬戶盧孛一人，千戶十餘人。

translations.literal: De crossed the river, struck, and recovered it; he pursued to Sangen, captured one Jurchen commander of ten thousand households named Lu Bo, and more than ten commanders of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De crossed the river, struck back, and recovered the city. He pursued as far as Sangen, captured the Jurchen commander of ten thousand households Lu Bo, and more than ten commanders of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五年，改環慶副總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made deputy overall commander of Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made deputy overall commander of the Huanqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，劉豫遣麟、猊驅鄉兵三十萬，分東西道入寇，中外甚恐，議欲為保江計。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year Liu Yu sent Lin and Ni driving three hundred thousand local militia in two columns, east and west, to invade; court and country were greatly afraid; some proposed plans merely to hold the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year Liu Yu sent Lin and Ni at the head of three hundred thousand local militia in eastern and western columns. Court and country were terrified, and some urged a plan merely to defend the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 殿帥楊沂中、統制張宗顏、田師中及德等分兵禦之，大敗猊兵於藕塘，猊挺身走；

translations.literal: Palace commander Yang Yizhong, controllers Zhang Zongyan and Tian Shizhong, and De and others divided their forces to resist; they routed Ni's army at Outang; Ni himself fled;
translations.idiomatic: Palace commander Yang Yizhong, controllers Zhang Zongyan and Tian Shizhong, and Wang De and others divided their forces to resist. They routed Ni's army at Outang, and Ni himself fled;

sentences.zh: 麟在順昌聞之，亦拔砦遁。

translations.literal: Lin at Shunchang heard of it and also abandoned his camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin at Shunchang heard of it, he too abandoned his camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 德追至壽春，弗及，獲其糧舟四百艘。

translations.literal: De pursued to Shouchun but did not overtake them; he captured four hundred of their grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De pursued as far as Shouchun but could not catch them. He did seize four hundred of their grain boats.

sentences.zh: 第功，除武康軍承宣使，真拜相州觀察使。

translations.literal: For his merit in rank he was made commissioner of the Wukang Army and formally appointed observer of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made commissioner of the Wukang Army and formally appointed observer of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，改熙河蘭廓路副總管、行營左護軍都統制，駐師合肥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made deputy overall commander of the Xihe, Lan, and Kuo circuit and overall commander of the Left Guard Army of the field headquarters, and stationed his army at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made deputy overall commander of the Xihe-Lan-Kuo circuit and overall commander of the Left Guard Army in the field headquarters, with his army at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 會光世罷宣撫，詔德盡護其眾，以酈瓊副之。

translations.literal: When Guangshi was removed as pacification commissioner, an edict ordered De to take charge of all his troops, with Li Qiong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Guangshi was dismissed as pacification commissioner, an edict ordered Wang De to take over all his troops, with Li Qiong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 瓊與德故等夷，恥屈其下，率眾叛從劉豫。

translations.literal: Qiong had formerly been De's equal; he was ashamed to serve under him and led his troops in rebellion to join Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong had once been Wang De's equal and was ashamed to serve under him. He led his troops in rebellion to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 八年，命隸張俊，名其軍曰「銳勝」。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to serve under Zhang Jun; his army was named "Sharp Victory."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was placed under Zhang Jun, and his army was named Sharp Victory.

sentences.zh: 十年，解潁昌圍，俊檄德就取宿州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he raised the siege of Yingchang; Jun ordered De to go and take Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he lifted the siege of Yingchang. Zhang Jun ordered Wang De to go and take Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 德倍道自壽春馳至蘄縣，與敵遊騎遇，遂入城，偃旗臥鼓，騎引去。

translations.literal: De marched by double stages from Shouchun to Qixian; he met enemy scouts, entered the city, lowered the flags and stilled the drums, and the scouts withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De forced the pace from Shouchun to Qixian. He met enemy scouts, entered the city, lowered the flags and stilled the drums, and the scouts withdrew.

sentences.zh: 因潛師宿州，夜半，薄賊營。

translations.literal: He then moved his army secretly to Suzhou; at midnight he pressed close to the bandit camp.
translations.idiomatic: He then stole a march on Suzhou and at midnight pressed close to the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 敵將高統軍詰朝壓汴而陳，偽守馬秦、同知耶律溫以三千人陰水邀戰。

translations.literal: The enemy general Gao the Commander-in-Chief at dawn pressed toward Bian and drew up his line; the false prefect Ma Qin and vice commissioner Yelü Wen with three thousand men lay in ambush by the water to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Commander Gao at dawn pressed toward Bian and drew up his line. The puppet prefect Ma Qin and vice commissioner Yelü Wen lay in ambush by the water with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 德策馬先濟，步騎從之。

translations.literal: De spurred his horse and crossed first; infantry and cavalry followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De spurred his horse and crossed first; infantry and cavalry followed.

sentences.zh: 遙謂賊曰：「吾與金人大小百戰，雖名王貴酋，莫不糜碎，爾何為者。

translations.literal: From afar he called to the bandits, "I have fought the Jurchens in a hundred great and small battles; even famous kings and noble chieftains have all been crushed to pulp—what are you doing?"
translations.idiomatic: From afar he shouted to the rebels, "I have fought the Jin in a hundred battles great and small. Even their princes and noble chiefs have been crushed to pulp—what are you doing here?"

sentences.zh: 」賊遂投兵降。

translations.literal: The bandits then cast down their weapons and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then cast down their weapons and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 馬秦、耶律溫馳入，閉門城守。

translations.literal: Ma Qin and Yelü Wen galloped into the city, shut the gates, and held the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qin and Yelü Wen galloped into the city, shut the gates, and held the walls.

sentences.zh: 德至，呼秦諭以逆順，乃自縋而下。

translations.literal: When De arrived he called to Qin and instructed him on loyalty and rebellion; Qin then lowered himself by rope and came down.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang De arrived he called to Ma Qin and lectured him on loyalty and rebellion. Ma Qin then let himself down by rope.

sentences.zh: 德叱其子順先登，秦率溫降，遣詣行在。

translations.literal: De ordered his son Shun to climb up first; Qin led Wen in surrender and sent them to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De ordered his son Shun to climb up first. Ma Qin brought Wen down in surrender and sent them to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 德乘勝趨亳州，俊會于城父。

translations.literal: De pressed his victory and hastened to Bozhou; Jun joined him at Chengfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De pressed his victory and hurried to Bozhou, where Zhang Jun joined him at Chengfu.

sentences.zh: 時叛將酈瓊屯亳，聞德至，謂三路都統制曰：「夜叉未易當也。

translations.literal: At the time the rebel general Li Qiong was stationed at Bo; when he heard that De had come he said to the three-route overall commanders, "The Yaksha is not easy to withstand."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Li Qiong was then at Bo. When he heard that Wang De had arrived, he told the three-route commanders, "That Yaksha is not easy to face."

sentences.zh: 」遂遁。

translations.literal: He then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fled.

sentences.zh: 德入亳州，白俊曰：「今兵威已振，請乘破竹之勢，進取東都。

translations.literal: De entered Bozhou and reported to Jun, "Now our military prestige is already roused; I ask that we take advantage of the momentum of splitting bamboo and advance to seize the Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: Wang De entered Bozhou and told Zhang Jun, "Our army's prestige is already high. I ask that we ride this momentum and advance on the Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 」俊難之，乃班師。

translations.literal: Jun found it difficult and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun hesitated, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 策功第一，拜興甯軍承宣使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使，再遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候，封隴西郡侯。

translations.literal: His merit was ranked first; he was made commissioner of the Xingning Army and commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, then transferred again to chief adjutant of the palace horse and foot armies, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was ranked first. He was made commissioner of the Xingning Army and commander of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, then promoted to chief adjutant of the palace horse and foot armies and enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，金人自合肥入侵，游騎及江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Jurchens invaded from Hefei; their scouts reached the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Jin invaded from Hefei, and their scouts reached the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 俊議分軍守南岸，德曰：「淮者，江之蔽也，棄淮不守，是謂唇亡齒寒也。

translations.literal: Jun proposed dividing the army to hold the south bank; De said, "The Huai is the screen of the Yangtze; to abandon the Huai and not defend it is what is called when the lips are gone the teeth grow cold."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun proposed dividing the army to hold the south bank. Wang De said, "The Huai is the Yangtze's shield. To abandon the Huai and not defend it is what people mean when they say that when the lips are gone the teeth grow cold."

sentences.zh: 敵數千里遠來，餉道決不繼，及其未濟急擊之，可以奪氣；

translations.literal: The enemy has come from thousands of li away; their supply route certainly cannot be sustained; while they have not yet crossed, strike them urgently and you can seize their spirit;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has marched thousands of li from home. Their supply line cannot possibly hold. Strike them hard before they finish crossing and you can break their spirit;

sentences.zh: 若遲之，使稍安，則淮非吾有矣」俊猶豫未許。

translations.literal: if you delay and let them settle somewhat, then the Huai will no longer be ours." Jun hesitated and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: if you delay and let them settle in, the Huai will no longer be ours." Zhang Jun hesitated and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 德請益堅，曰：「願父子先越江，俟和州下，然後宣撫北渡。

translations.literal: De pressed his request more firmly and said, "I wish that father and son cross the river first; when He Prefecture is taken, then the pacification commissioner may cross north."
translations.idiomatic: Wang De pressed harder and said, "Let my son and I cross the river first. When Hezhou falls, then the pacification commissioner may cross north."

sentences.zh: 」俊乃許德即渡採石，俊督軍繼之。

translations.literal: Jun then allowed De to cross at once from Caishi; Jun supervised the army and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun then let Wang De cross at once from Caishi while he followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 宿江中，德曰：「明旦，當會食曆陽。

translations.literal: They lodged on the river; De said, "Tomorrow morning we shall meet to eat at Liyang."
translations.idiomatic: They spent the night on the river. Wang De said, "Tomorrow morning we shall breakfast together at Liyang."

sentences.zh: 」已而夜拔和州，晨迎俊入。

translations.literal: Then by night he stormed He Prefecture; at dawn he welcomed Jun in.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stormed Hezhou, and at dawn he welcomed Zhang Jun into the city.

sentences.zh: 敵退保昭關，又擊走之，追至柘皋，與金人夾河而軍。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew to hold Zhaoguan; he struck and drove them off again, pursued to Zhegao, and encamped facing the Jurchens across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back to hold Zhaoguan. He struck again and drove them off, pursued to Zhegao, and encamped facing the Jin across the river.

sentences.zh: 諸將帥皆集，惟張俊後至，統制田師中欲待之，德怒曰：「事當機會，復何待！

translations.literal: All the generals had assembled; only Zhang Jun arrived late; the controller Tian Shizhong wished to wait for him; De said angrily, "Matters depend on the moment—why wait again!"
translations.idiomatic: All the generals had assembled; only Zhang Jun was late. Controller Tian Shizhong wanted to wait for him. Wang De said angrily, "This turns on the moment—why wait again!"

sentences.zh: 」徑上馬。

translations.literal: He mounted his horse straightway.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted at once.

sentences.zh: 兀朮以鐵騎十余萬夾道而陣，德曰：「賊右陣堅，我當先擊之。

translations.literal: Wuzhu drew up more than a hundred thousand iron cavalry along both sides of the road; De said, "The enemy's right wing is strong; I should strike it first."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu drew up more than a hundred thousand armored cavalry along both sides of the road. Wang De said, "Their right wing is strong—we should strike it first."

sentences.zh: 」麾軍渡橋，首犯其鋒。

translations.literal: He ordered the army across the bridge and was the first to strike their front.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army across the bridge and was the first to strike their front.

sentences.zh: 一酋被甲躍馬始出，德引弓一發而斃；

translations.literal: One chieftain in armor leaped forth on his horse as he came out; De drew his bow and with one shot laid him dead;
translations.idiomatic: One chieftain in armor leaped out on his horse; Wang De drew his bow and dropped him with a single shot;

sentences.zh: 乘勝大呼，令萬兵持長斧，如牆而進。

translations.literal: pressing the victory he shouted loudly and ordered ten thousand men to take long axes and advance like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: pressing the victory he shouted and ordered ten thousand men to take long axes and advance like a moving wall.

sentences.zh: 敵大敗，退屯紫金山，德復尾擊之。

translations.literal: The enemy was utterly defeated and withdrew to encamp at Purple Gold Mountain; De again struck them from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was routed and fell back to Purple Gold Mountain. Wang De struck them again from the rear.

sentences.zh: 劉錡謂德曰：「昔聞公威略如神，今果見之，請以兄禮事。

translations.literal: Liu Qi said to De, "Long ago I heard that your martial prestige and strategy were like a god's; today I truly see it; I ask to serve you with the rites due an elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi told Wang De, "I have long heard that your martial prestige and strategy were godlike. Today I have seen it for myself. I ask to treat you with the courtesy due an elder brother."

sentences.zh: 」召拜清遠軍節度使、建康府駐劄御前諸軍都統制，曆浙東福建總管、荊南副都統制。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and overall commander of all armies stationed before the throne at Jiankang Prefecture; he served in turn as overall administrator of Zhedong and Fujian and as deputy overall commander of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and made military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army and overall commander of all imperial armies stationed at Jiankang. He later served as overall administrator of Zhedong and Fujian and as deputy overall commander of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，贈檢校少保，再贈少傅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died; he was posthumously given the checked rank of Junior Guardian and later Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died. He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and later Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 二子琪、順，亦以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: His two sons Qi and Shun were also known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Qi and Shun were also famed for their fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 王彥，字子才，上黨人。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Zicai, was a man of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, styled Zicai, came from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 性豪縱，喜讀韜略。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and unrestrained and delighted in reading military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and unrestrained and loved to read works on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 父奇之，使詣京師，隸弓馬子弟所。

translations.literal: His father thought him remarkable and sent him to the capital to be attached to the Institute of Archery and Horsemanship.
translations.idiomatic: His father thought him remarkable and sent him to the capital, where he was enrolled in the Institute of Archery and Horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 徽宗臨軒閱試，補下班祗應，為清河尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong reviewed the examination in the hall, he was appointed attendant of the lower shift and made captain of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong reviewed the examination in the hall, he was appointed an attendant of the lower shift and made captain of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 從涇原路經略使種師道兩入夏國，有戰功。

translations.literal: He followed the Jingyuan circuit commissioner Zhong Shidao twice into the Western Xia and won battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Jingyuan circuit commissioner Zhong Shidao on two campaigns into the Western Xia and won distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 金人攻汴京，彥慨然棄家赴闕，求自試討賊。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Bianjing, Yan left his family in high spirit and went to the court, asking to prove himself in suppressing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Bianjing, Wang Yan left his family behind and went to court, asking for a chance to prove himself against the invaders.

sentences.zh: 時張所為河北招撫使，異其才，擢為都統制。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Suo was pacification commissioner of Hebei; he was struck by Yan's talent and promoted him to overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suo was then pacification commissioner of Hebei. Impressed by Wang Yan's talent, he promoted him to overall commander.

sentences.zh: 使率裨將張翼、白安民、岳飛等十一將，部七千人渡河，與金人戰。

translations.literal: He was sent to lead the deputy generals Zhang Yi, Bai Anmin, Yue Fei, and eleven other commanders with seven thousand men across the river to fight the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to lead deputy generals Zhang Yi, Bai Anmin, Yue Fei, and ten other commanders with seven thousand men across the river to fight the Jin.

sentences.zh: 敗之，復衛州新鄉縣，傳檄諸郡。

translations.literal: He defeated them, recovered Xinxiang County in Weizhou, and sent proclamations to the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them, recovered Xinxiang County in Weizhou, and sent proclamations to the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 金人以為大軍至，率數萬眾薄彥壘，圍之數匝。

translations.literal: The Jurchens thought a great army had arrived; they led tens of thousands to press Yan's camp and surrounded it in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin thought a great army had arrived. They brought tens of thousands against Wang Yan's camp and surrounded it layer upon layer.

sentences.zh: 彥以眾寡不敵，潰圍出。

translations.literal: Yan, seeing that his numbers could not match theirs, broke through the encirclement and got out.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he was outnumbered, Wang Yan broke through the encirclement and escaped.

sentences.zh: 諸將散歸，彥獨保共城西山，遣腹心結兩河豪傑，圖再舉。

translations.literal: The generals scattered and returned; Yan alone held the western hills of Gongcheng, sent trusted men to rally the magnates of the two Hebei circuits, and planned to rise again.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals scattered homeward. Wang Yan alone held the western hills of Gongcheng, sent trusted men to rally the magnates of the two Hebei circuits, and planned to rise again.

sentences.zh: 金人購求彥急，彥慮變，夜寢屢遷。

translations.literal: The Jurchens urgently offered a price for Yan's capture; Yan feared treachery and moved his sleeping place many times each night.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin urgently offered a reward for Wang Yan's capture. Fearing betrayal, he changed his sleeping place many times each night.

sentences.zh: 其部曲覺之，相率刺面，作「赤心報國，誓殺金賊」八字，以示無他意。

translations.literal: His personal troops noticed this; they all tattooed their faces with the eight characters "Loyal heart to serve the state, sworn to kill the Jin bandits" to show they had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: His personal troops noticed this. They tattooed their faces with the eight characters "Loyal heart to serve the state, sworn to kill the Jin bandits" to show they had no other intent.

sentences.zh: 彥益感勵，撫愛士卒，與同甘苦。

translations.literal: Yan was all the more moved and encouraged; he cherished his soldiers and shared their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was deeply moved. He cherished his soldiers and shared their hardships.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兩河回應，忠義民兵首領傅選、孟德、劉澤、焦文通等皆附之，眾十余萬，綿亙數百里，皆受彥約束。

translations.literal: Before long the two Hebei circuits responded; the loyal militia leaders Fu Xuan, Meng De, Liu Ze, Jiao Wentong, and others all attached themselves to him; his forces numbered more than a hundred thousand, stretching for several hundred li, all under Yan's command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the two Hebei circuits answered his call. Loyal militia leaders Fu Xuan, Meng De, Liu Ze, Jiao Wentong, and others joined him. His forces numbered more than a hundred thousand and stretched for hundreds of li, all under Wang Yan's command.

sentences.zh: 金人患之，召其首領，俾以大兵破彥壘。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were troubled by this; they summoned their chieftains and ordered them to break Yan's camp with a great army.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were alarmed. They summoned their chieftains and ordered them to break Wang Yan's camp with a great army.

sentences.zh: 首領跪而泣曰：「王都統砦堅如鐵石，未易圖也。

translations.literal: The chieftains knelt and wept, saying, "Commander Wang's stockade is firm as iron and stone; it is not easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains knelt and wept, saying, "Commander Wang's stockade is firm as iron and stone. It is not easy to take."

sentences.zh: 」金人乃間遣勁騎撓彥糧道，彥勒兵待之，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The Jurchens then secretly sent crack cavalry to harass Yan's supply route; Yan held his troops in readiness and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin then secretly sent crack cavalry to harass Wang Yan's supply lines. He held his troops ready and killed or captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 益治兵，刻日大舉，告期於東京留守宗澤。

translations.literal: He trained his troops all the more, set a day for a great campaign, and informed Zong Ze, defender of the Eastern Capital, of the date.
translations.idiomatic: He trained his troops harder, set a date for a major campaign, and informed Zong Ze, defender of the Eastern Capital, when he would move.

sentences.zh: 澤召彥會議，乃將兵萬餘渡河，金人以重兵襲其後而不敢擊。

translations.literal: Ze summoned Yan for counsel; Yan then led more than ten thousand troops across the river; the Jurchens sent a heavy force to strike his rear but did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze summoned Wang Yan for counsel. Wang Yan then led more than ten thousand troops across the river. The Jin sent a heavy force against his rear but did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 既至汴京，澤大喜，令彥宿兵近甸，以衛根本。

translations.literal: When he reached Bianjing, Ze was greatly pleased and ordered Yan to encamp in the nearby countryside to guard the root of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Bianjing, Zong Ze was overjoyed and ordered Wang Yan to encamp in the nearby countryside to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 彥即以所部兵馬付留守司，量帶親兵趨行在。

translations.literal: Yan then handed over the troops and horses under his command to the defender's office and, taking only a portion of his personal guard, hastened to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan then handed his troops over to the defender's office and, taking only a portion of his personal guard, hurried to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 時已遣宇文虛中為祈請使議和。

translations.literal: At the time Yuwen Xuzhong had already been sent as petition envoy to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xuzhong had already been sent as petition envoy to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 彥見黃潛善、汪伯彥，力陳兩河忠義延頸以望王師，願因人心，大舉北伐。

translations.literal: Yan saw Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan and forcefully stated that the loyal men of the two Hebei circuits craned their necks awaiting the imperial army; he wished to take advantage of popular sentiment and launch a great northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan saw Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan and argued forcefully that the loyal men of the two Hebei circuits were waiting eagerly for the imperial army. He urged a great northern expedition while popular sentiment was on their side.

sentences.zh: 言辭憤激，大忤時相意，遂降旨免對，以彥為武翼郎、閣門宣贊舍人，差充禦營平寇統領。

translations.literal: His words were impassioned and greatly offended the chief minister; an edict was then issued excusing him from audience; Yan was made Military Wing Gentleman and Palace Gate Proclamation Attendant and assigned as commander to pacify bandits in the Imperial Camp.
translations.idiomatic: His words were impassioned and greatly offended the chief minister. An edict excused him from further audience. Wang Yan was made Military Wing Gentleman and Palace Gate Proclamation Attendant and assigned to pacify bandits in the Imperial Camp.

sentences.zh: 時范瓊為平寇前將軍，彥知瓊有逆節，稱疾不就，乞致仕，許之。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Qiong was forward general for pacifying bandits; Yan knew Qiong harbored treasonous intent, pleaded illness and refused the post, asked to retire, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiong was then forward general for pacifying bandits. Wang Yan knew Fan harbored treasonous intent, pleaded illness, refused the post, asked to retire, and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事張浚宣撫川、陝，奏彥為前軍統制。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was pacification commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi; he memorialized that Yan be made controller of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was pacification commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi. He recommended Wang Yan as controller of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 浚與金酋婁宿相持于富平，欲大舉，初至漢中，會諸將議，彥獨以為不可，曰：「陝西兵將上下之情，皆未相通，若少不利，則五路俱失。

translations.literal: Jun was locked in stalemate with the Jurchen chieftain Lou Su at Fuping and wished to launch a great campaign; when he first reached Hanzhong he met the generals in council; Yan alone thought it impossible and said, "In Shaanxi the feelings between officers and men above and below are not yet united; if there is the slightest setback, all five routes will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was locked in stalemate with the Jurchen chieftain Lou Su at Fuping and wanted a major campaign. When he first reached Hanzhong he met the generals in council. Wang Yan alone objected and said, "In Shaanxi the bond between officers and men is not yet firm. One setback and all five routes will be lost."

sentences.zh: 不若且屯利、閬、興、洋，以固根本，敵入境，則檄五路兵來援，萬一不捷，未大失也。

translations.literal: It would be better to encamp for the time being at Li, Lang, Xing, and Yang to secure the root; when the enemy enters our territory, issue orders to the five routes to come to our aid; if by chance we do not succeed, the loss will not be great."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold Li, Lang, Xing, and Yang for now and secure our base. When the enemy enters our territory, summon the five routes to reinforce us. Even if we fail, the loss will not be catastrophic."

sentences.zh: 」浚幕府不然其言。

translations.literal: Jun's staff did not agree with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun's staff did not agree.

sentences.zh: 彥即請為利路鈐轄，俄改金均房州安撫使、知金州。

translations.literal: Yan then asked to be made military intendant of the Li circuit; shortly thereafter he was changed to pacification commissioner of Jin, Jun, and Fang prefectures and prefect of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan then asked to be made military intendant of the Li circuit. Shortly thereafter he was made pacification commissioner of Jin, Jun, and Fang prefectures and prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時中原盜賊蜂起，加以饑饉，無所資食；

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed across the central plains, and famine was added besides; there was nothing with which to sustain life;
translations.idiomatic: Bandits swarmed across the central plains, and famine made matters worse. There was nothing with which to live;

sentences.zh: 惟蜀富饒，巨盜往往窺覬。

translations.literal: only Shu was rich and abundant, and great bandits often cast covetous eyes upon it.
translations.idiomatic: only Shu was rich and abundant, and great bandits often cast covetous eyes upon it.

sentences.zh: 桑仲既陷淮安、襄陽，乘勢西向，均、房失守，直搗金州白土關，眾號三十萬。

translations.literal: Sang Zhong had already taken Huai'an and Xiangyang; riding the momentum he turned west; Jun and Fang were lost; he drove straight at Baitu Pass in Jin Prefecture; his forces were said to number three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Zhong had already taken Huai'an and Xiangyang. Riding the momentum he turned west. Jun and Fang fell, and he drove straight at Baitu Pass in Jinzhou. His forces were said to number three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 仲，彥舊部曲也，以申櫝請於彥曰：「仲於公無敢犯，願假道入蜀就食耳。

translations.literal: Zhong had been Yan's old personal troop; he sent a petition in a casket asking Yan, "Zhong would not dare offend you, sir; I only wish to borrow the road into Shu to seek food."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong had once served under Wang Yan. He sent a petition asking, "I would not dare offend you, sir. I only wish to pass through your territory into Shu to find food."

sentences.zh: 」彥乃遣統領官門立為先鋒擊之。

translations.literal: Yan then sent the commander Men Li as vanguard to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan then sent commander Men Li as vanguard to strike him.

sentences.zh: 賊銳甚，立戰死。

translations.literal: The bandits were very sharp; Li died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were very fierce, and Men Li was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 將士失色，或請避之。

translations.literal: The officers and men turned pale; some asked to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men turned pale. Some urged retreat.

sentences.zh: 彥叱曰：「樞相張公方有事關陝，若仲越金而至梁、洋，則腹背受敵，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Yan shouted, "Chief Councillor Zhang is already occupied in Guan and Shaanxi; if Zhong crosses the Jin territory and reaches Liang and Yang, we will be attacked front and rear and the great affair will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan shouted, "Chief Councillor Zhang is already occupied in Shaanxi. If Zhong crosses Jin territory and reaches Liang and Yang, we will be attacked front and rear and the great cause will be lost."

sentences.zh: 敢言避者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak of avoiding them shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever dares speak of retreat shall be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 」即勒兵趨長沙平，阻水據山，設伏以待。

translations.literal: He then led his troops to Changshaping, blocked the water and held the hills, and set ambushes to wait.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops to Changshaping, blocked the water and held the hills, and set ambushes to wait.

sentences.zh: 賊見官軍少，蟻附搏戰。

translations.literal: The bandits saw that the government troops were few and swarmed up to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw that the government troops were few and swarmed up to fight.

sentences.zh: 彥執幟一麾，士殊死鬥，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Yan seized the banner and waved it once; the men fought to the death; the bandits were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan seized the banner and waved it once. His men fought to the death. The rebels were routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 彥休士進擊，追奔至白磧，復房州。

translations.literal: Yan rested his men and pressed the attack, pursued the fugitives to Baiqi, and recovered Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan rested his men and pressed the attack, pursued the fugitives to Baiqi, and recovered Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，桑仲既敗還襄陽，乃鳩集散亡陷鄧州，兇焰復熾。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Sang Zhong was defeated and returned to Xiangyang, he gathered the scattered and lost, took Deng Prefecture, and his ferocity flared up again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Sang Zhong was defeated and returned to Xiangyang, he gathered the scattered survivors, took Dengzhou, and his power flared up again.

sentences.zh: 南攻德安，西據均陽，分眾三道：一攻住口關，一出馬郎嶺，一搗洵陽，前軍去金州不三十里。

translations.literal: He attacked De'an in the south and held Junyang in the west, dividing his forces in three columns: one attacked Zhukou Pass, one came out at Malang Ridge, one struck Xunyang; the vanguard was less than thirty li from Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked De'an in the south and held Junyang in the west, dividing his forces in three columns: one attacked Zhukou Pass, one came out at Malang Ridge, one struck Xunyang. The vanguard was less than thirty li from Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥曰：「仲以我寡彼眾，故分三道以離吾勢，法當先破其堅，則脆者自走。

translations.literal: Yan said, "Zhong, seeing that we are few and they are many, has therefore divided into three routes to disperse our strength; by rule we should first break their strong point, and the weak will flee of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan said, "Zhong, seeing that we are few and they are many, has divided into three columns to disperse our strength. We should break their strongest point first, and the weaker columns will flee on their own."

sentences.zh: 」遣副將焦文通禦住口，自以親兵營馬郎。

translations.literal: He sent the deputy general Jiao Wentong to hold Zhukou and himself encamped with his personal troops at Malang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent deputy general Jiao Wentong to hold Zhukou and himself encamped with his personal troops at Malang.

sentences.zh: 相持一月，大戰六日，賊大敗，仲為其下所殺。

translations.literal: They faced each other for a month; great battles were fought for six days; the bandits were utterly defeated; Zhong was killed by his own men.
translations.idiomatic: They faced each other for a month. After six days of heavy fighting the rebels were routed, and Zhong was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 又有王辟、董貴、祁守中阻兵窺蜀，勢雖不及桑仲，然小者猶不減數萬，彥悉討平之。

translations.literal: There were also Wang Pi, Dong Gui, and Qi Shouzhong, who blocked the roads with troops and cast eyes on Shu; though their power did not match Sang Zhong's, even the smaller bands were no less than tens of thousands; Yan pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, Dong Gui, and Qi Shouzhong also blocked the roads with troops and cast eyes on Shu. Though their power did not match Sang Zhong's, even the smaller bands numbered tens of thousands. Wang Yan pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 是冬，偽齊秦鳳經略使郭振以數千騎掠白石鎮，彥與關師古並兵禦之，賊大敗，獲振，復秦州。

translations.literal: That winter Guo Zhen, commissioner of Qin and Feng for the false Qi, raided Baishi Stockade with several thousand horsemen; Yan and Guan Shigu joined forces to resist; the bandits were utterly defeated; Zhen was captured and Qin Prefecture recovered.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Guo Zhen, commissioner of Qin and Feng for the puppet Qi state, raided Baishi Stockade with several thousand horsemen. Wang Yan and Guan Shigu joined forces to resist, routed the enemy, captured Zhen, and recovered Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 張浚承制以彥節制商、虢、陝、華州軍馬。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, acting on imperial commission, placed Yan in command of the troops and horses of Shang, Guo, Shan, and Hua prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, acting on imperial commission, placed Wang Yan in command of the troops and horses of Shang, Guo, Shan, and Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，兀朮入侵，浚召彥與吳玠、劉子羽會於興元。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Wuzhu invaded; Jun summoned Yan, Wu Jie, and Liu Ziyu to meet at Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Wuzhu invaded. Zhang Jun summoned Wang Yan, Wu Jie, and Liu Ziyu to meet at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 撒離曷自上津疾馳，不一日至洵陽。

translations.literal: Salihe galloped from Shangjin and reached Xunyang in less than a day.
translations.idiomatic: Salihe galloped from Shangjin and reached Xunyang in less than a day.

sentences.zh: 統制官郭進死之，彥退保石泉縣。

translations.literal: The controller Guo Jin died in the fighting; Yan withdrew to hold Shiquan County.
translations.idiomatic: Controller Guo Jin was killed. Wang Yan withdrew to hold Shiquan County.

sentences.zh: 金人入金、均，彥趨西鄉。

translations.literal: The Jurchens entered Jin and Jun; Yan hastened to Xixiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin entered Jin and Jun prefectures. Wang Yan hastened to Xixiang.

sentences.zh: 二月，金人攻饒風關，彥與吳玠禦之，不能卻，關破，彥收余兵奔達州。

translations.literal: In the second month the Jurchens attacked Raofeng Pass; Yan and Wu Jie resisted but could not drive them back; the pass fell; Yan gathered his remaining troops and fled to Da Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Jin attacked Raofeng Pass. Wang Yan and Wu Jie resisted but could not drive them back. The pass fell. Wang Yan gathered his remaining troops and fled to Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，彥遣兵至漢陰縣，與劉豫將周貴戰，大敗之，復金州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Yan sent troops to Hanyin County, fought Liu Yu's general Zhou Gui, utterly defeated him, and recovered Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wang Yan sent troops to Hanyin County, fought Liu Yu's general Zhou Gui, routed him, and recovered Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚承制進彥保康軍承宣使兼宣撫司參議，彥不受。

translations.literal: Jun, acting on commission, promoted Yan to commissioner of the Baokang Army and staff adviser to the pacification office; Yan did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, acting on commission, promoted Wang Yan to commissioner of the Baokang Army and staff adviser to the pacification office. Wang Yan declined.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，差知荊南府，充歸、峽、荊門公安軍安撫使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year he was assigned as prefect of Jingnan Prefecture and made pacification commissioner of Gui, Xia, Jingmen, and Gong'an armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year he was assigned as prefect of Jingnan and made pacification commissioner of the Gui, Xia, Jingmen, and Gong'an districts.

sentences.zh: 彥因荊南曠土措置屯田，自蜀買牛千七百頭，授官兵耕，營田八百五十頃，分給將士有差。

translations.literal: Yan, because of the vacant land in Jingnan, arranged garrison fields; he bought seventeen hundred oxen from Shu, gave them to officers and soldiers to farm, opened eight hundred fifty qing of fields, and distributed them to the generals and troops in varying shares.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the vacant land in Jingnan, Wang Yan organized garrison farming. He bought seventeen hundred oxen from Shu, gave them to officers and soldiers to farm, opened eight hundred fifty qing of fields, and distributed them to the troops in varying shares.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，知襄陽府、京西南路安撫使，彥以岳飛嫌辭。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year he was made prefect of Xiangyang and pacification commissioner of the southwestern capital circuit; Yan declined because of Yue Fei's resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he was made prefect of Xiangyang and pacification commissioner of the southwestern capital circuit. Wang Yan declined because of Yue Fei's resentment.

sentences.zh: 浚奏彥為行營前護副軍都統制、督府參謀軍事。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized that Yan be made deputy overall commander of the Forward Guard Army of the field headquarters and military adviser on the staff of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun recommended Wang Yan as deputy overall commander of the Forward Guard Army in the field headquarters and military adviser on the command staff.

sentences.zh: 六月，以八字軍萬人赴行在。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he led ten thousand men of the Eight-Character Army to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he led ten thousand men of the Eight-Character Army to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 至鎮江，聞母喪，上疏乞解官，不許。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhenjiang he heard of his mother's death; he submitted a memorial asking to resign his office; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhenjiang he heard of his mother's death and submitted a memorial asking to resign. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 詔免喪服，趣入對，遂以為浙西、淮東沿海制置副使，以所部屯通州之料角。

translations.literal: An edict excused him from mourning garb and urged him to enter audience; he was then made deputy commissioner for the coastal defense of Zhexi and Huaidong, and his troops were stationed at Liaojiao in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict excused him from mourning and urged him to audience. He was then made deputy commissioner for coastal defense of Zhexi and Huaidong, and his troops were stationed at Liaojiao in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，彥因遣將捕亡者于解潛軍中，軍士交鬥于市，言者論其軍政不肅，貶秩二等。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Yan, because he sent a general to capture deserters in Xie Qian's army, had soldiers brawl in the market; critics argued that his military discipline was lax; his rank was reduced by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year Wang Yan sent a general to capture deserters in Xie Qian's army. His soldiers brawled in the market. Critics argued that his military discipline was lax, and his rank was reduced by two grades.

sentences.zh: 彥不自安，乞終餘服。

translations.literal: Yan was ill at ease and asked to complete the remainder of his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was ill at ease and asked to complete his mourning period.

sentences.zh: 二月，復洪州觀察使、知邵州。

translations.literal: In the second month he was restored as observer of Hong Prefecture and prefect of Shao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was restored as observer of Hongzhou and prefect of Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 彥入辭，帝撫勞甚厚，曰：「以卿能牧民，故付卿便郡，行即召矣。

translations.literal: Yan entered to take leave; the emperor comforted and rewarded him very generously and said, "Because you can govern the people, I have given you a convenient prefecture; you will soon be summoned back."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan came to take leave. The emperor comforted and rewarded him generously and said, "Because you can govern the people well, I have given you a convenient prefecture. You will soon be summoned back."

sentences.zh: 」九年，卒於官，年五十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died in office at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he died in office at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 彥稱名將，當建炎初，屢破大敵，威聲振河朔。

translations.literal: Yan was called a famous general; at the beginning of the Jianyan era he repeatedly defeated great enemies, and his martial renown shook Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was accounted a famous general. At the beginning of the Jianyan era he repeatedly defeated major enemies, and his martial renown shook Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時方撓於和議，遽召之還，又奪其兵柄而使之治郡，士議惜之。

translations.literal: At the time the court was yielding to peace talks; he was suddenly summoned back, and his military authority was taken away and he was made to govern a prefecture; scholars regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then yielding to peace talks. He was suddenly recalled, stripped of military command, and made to govern a prefecture. Scholars regretted the waste of his talent.

sentences.zh: 彥事親孝，居官廉，子弟有戰功，不與推賞。

translations.literal: Yan was filial to his parents and incorrupt in office; when his sons and younger brothers won battle merit he did not recommend them for reward.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was filial to his parents and incorrupt in office. When his sons and younger brothers won battle merit he did not recommend them for reward.

sentences.zh: 將死，召其弟侄，以家財均給之。

translations.literal: When he was about to die he summoned his younger brothers and nephews and divided his family property equally among them.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to die he summoned his younger brothers and nephews and divided his family property equally among them.

sentences.zh: 魏勝，字彥威，淮陽軍宿遷縣人。

translations.literal: Wei Sheng, courtesy name Yanwei, was a man of Suqian County in Huaiyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng, styled Yanwei, came from Suqian County in the Huaiyang Army district.

sentences.zh: 多智勇，善騎射，應募為弓箭手，徙居山陽。

translations.literal: He had much wisdom and courage, was skilled in horsemanship and archery, enlisted as an archer, and moved his residence to Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was resourceful and brave, skilled in horsemanship and archery. He enlisted as an archer and moved to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年，金人將南侵，聚芻糧，造器械，籍諸路民為兵。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of the Shaoxing era the Jurchens were about to invade south; they gathered fodder and grain, made weapons, and registered the people of the various circuits as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of the Shaoxing era the Jin were about to invade the south. They gathered fodder and grain, made weapons, and registered the people of the various circuits as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 勝躍曰：「此其時也。

translations.literal: Sheng leaped up and said, "This is the time."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng leaped up and said, "This is the time."

sentences.zh: 」聚義士三百，北渡淮，取漣水軍，宣佈朝廷德意，不殺一人，漣水民翕然以聽。

translations.literal: He gathered three hundred righteous men, crossed the Huai northward, took Lianshui Army, proclaimed the court's benevolent intent, killed no one, and the people of Lianshui all submitted at once.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered three hundred loyal volunteers, crossed the Huai northward, took Lianshui, proclaimed the court's benevolent intent, killed no one, and the people of Lianshui submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 遂取海州。

translations.literal: He then took Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 郡守渤海高文富聞勝起，遣兵來捕勝。

translations.literal: The prefect Gao Wenfu of Bohai, hearing that Sheng had risen, sent troops to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Gao Wenfu of Bohai, hearing that Wei Sheng had risen, sent troops to capture him.

sentences.zh: 距海州南八十里大伊，與金兵遇，勝迎擊走之，追至城下。

translations.literal: At Dayi, eighty li south of Haizhou, he met Jin troops; Sheng met them in attack and drove them off, pursuing to the foot of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: At Dayi, eighty li south of Haizhou, he met Jin troops. Wei Sheng attacked and drove them off, pursuing to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 眾驚傳水陸悉有兵，城中大恐，文富閉門守，驅民上城禦之。

translations.literal: The crowd was alarmed; rumor spread that there were troops on land and water alike; the city was greatly afraid; Wenfu shut the gates and held the defense, driving the people up onto the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the city. Rumor said there were troops on land and water alike. The city was terrified. Wenfu shut the gates, held the defense, and drove the people onto the walls to resist.

sentences.zh: 勝令城外多張旗幟，舉煙火為疑兵；

translations.literal: Sheng ordered many banners displayed outside the city and raised smoke and fire as a decoy force;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng ordered many banners displayed outside the city and raised smoke and fire as a decoy force;

sentences.zh: 又遣人向諸城門，諭以金人棄信背盟，無名興師，本朝寬大愛民之意。

translations.literal: he also sent men to the various gates to proclaim that the Jurchens had broken faith and betrayed the alliance, had raised arms without cause, and to explain the court's magnanimity and love for the people.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent men to the gates to proclaim that the Jin had broken faith and betrayed the alliance, had raised arms without cause, and to explain the court's magnanimity toward the people.

sentences.zh: 城上民聞之，即開門，勝遣勇銳者登城樓，餘自門入，莫有禦者。

translations.literal: When the people on the walls heard this they opened the gates at once; Sheng sent the brave and sharp up onto the tower; the rest entered by the gates; no one resisted.
translations.idiomatic: When the people on the walls heard this they opened the gates. Wei Sheng sent his best fighters up onto the tower while the rest entered through the gates. No one resisted.

sentences.zh: 獨文富與其子安仁率牙兵拒守，勝整軍與安仁父子戰譙門內，殺安仁及州兵千余，擒文富，民皆按堵。

translations.literal: Only Wenfu and his son Anren led the guard troops in resistance; Sheng arrayed his army and fought Anren father and son inside the gate tower, killed Anren and more than a thousand prefectural troops, captured Wenfu, and the people were all at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wenfu and his son Anren led the guard troops in resistance. Wei Sheng arrayed his army and fought them inside the gate tower, killed Anren and more than a thousand prefectural troops, captured Wenfu, and the people were left in peace.

sentences.zh: 勝權知州事，遣人諭朐山、懷仁、沐陽、東海諸縣，皆定。

translations.literal: Sheng acted as provisional prefect and sent men to instruct Qushan, Huairen, Muyang, Donghai, and the other counties; all were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng acted as provisional prefect and sent men to Qushan, Huairen, Muyang, Donghai, and the other counties. All submitted.

sentences.zh: 乃蠲租銳，釋罪囚，發倉庫，犒戰士；

translations.literal: He then remitted harsh rents, released prisoners, opened the storehouses, and rewarded the fighting men;
translations.idiomatic: He remitted harsh rents, released prisoners, opened the storehouses, and rewarded his fighting men;

sentences.zh: 分忠義士為五軍，紀律明肅，部分如宿將。

translations.literal: he divided the righteous volunteers into five armies with clear and strict discipline, deploying them like a veteran general.
translations.idiomatic: he divided the loyal volunteers into five armies with clear, strict discipline, deploying them like a veteran general.

sentences.zh: 勝自兼都統制，益募忠義以圖收復，遠近聞之回應，旬日，得兵數千。

translations.literal: Sheng himself also served as overall commander; he recruited more righteous men to plan recovery; those near and far heard and responded; within ten days he had several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng also served as overall commander. He recruited more loyal volunteers to plan recovery. Men near and far heard and responded. Within ten days he had several thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 即具其事報境上帥守，冀給軍裝器甲。

translations.literal: He then reported the whole affair in detail to the commanders on the border, hoping they would supply military equipment and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported the whole affair to the border commanders, hoping they would supply arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 時帥守雖知金人將渝盟，未有發其端者，莫敢以聞。

translations.literal: At the time the commanders, though they knew the Jurchens were about to break the alliance, had not yet seen the first sign of it and did not dare report it.
translations.idiomatic: The border commanders knew the Jin were about to break the alliance, but no overt sign had yet appeared, and none dared report it.

sentences.zh: 左軍統制董成謀出西北取沂州，勝先遣間還，知金兵數萬至沂，以我軍器甲未備，戒成勿動。

translations.literal: Dong Cheng, controller of the left army, planned to go northwest and take Yizhou; Sheng first sent spies back and learned that tens of thousands of Jin troops had reached Yi; because our arms and armor were not ready, he warned Cheng not to move.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cheng, controller of the left army, planned to march northwest and take Yizhou. Wei Sheng sent spies back first and learned that tens of thousands of Jin troops had reached Yi. Because their arms and armor were not ready, he warned Cheng not to move.

sentences.zh: 成不從勝，率所部千餘人直入沂州巷戰，殺其守及軍士三千余，眾悉降，得器甲數萬。

translations.literal: Cheng did not obey Sheng; he led more than a thousand men of his command straight into Yizhou for street fighting, killed the defender and more than three thousand soldiers, all the rest surrendered, and he obtained tens of thousands of pieces of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng disobeyed. He led more than a thousand men straight into Yizhou for street fighting, killed the defender and more than three thousand soldiers, took the rest in surrender, and seized tens of thousands of pieces of armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 金人生兵復集，競登屋擲瓦擊之，成軍幾敗。

translations.literal: Fresh Jin troops gathered again; they scrambled onto roofs and hurled tiles at them; Cheng's army was nearly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh Jin troops gathered again. They scrambled onto roofs and hurled tiles down. Cheng's army was nearly defeated.

sentences.zh: 勝欲斬成，以其驍勇，釋之。

translations.literal: Sheng wished to behead Cheng but, because of his fierce valor, released him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng wanted to behead Cheng but spared him because of his fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 金人遣同知海州事蒙恬鎮國以兵萬餘取海州，抵州北二十里新橋。

translations.literal: The Jurchens sent Meng Tian Zhenguo, vice commissioner of Haizhou, with more than ten thousand troops to take Haizhou; they reached Xinqiao, twenty li north of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent Meng Tian Zhenguo, vice commissioner of Haizhou, with more than ten thousand troops to retake Haizhou. They reached Xinqiao, twenty li north of the city.

sentences.zh: 勝帥兵出迎之，設伏於隘，陣以待。

translations.literal: Sheng led his troops out to meet them, set ambushes in the pass, and drew up his line to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng led his troops out to meet them, set ambushes in the pass, and drew up his line to wait.

sentences.zh: 眾殊死戰，伏發，賊大敗，殺鎮國，馘千人，降三百人，軍聲益振。

translations.literal: The men fought to the death; the ambush sprang; the bandits were utterly defeated; Zhenguo was killed; a thousand heads were taken; three hundred surrendered; the army's renown rose all the more.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought to the death. The ambush sprang. The enemy was routed. Zhenguo was killed, a thousand heads were taken, and three hundred men surrendered. The army's renown rose still higher.

sentences.zh: 山東之民鹹欲來附，勝傳檄招諭，結集以待王師之至。

translations.literal: The people of Shandong all wished to come and attach themselves; Sheng sent proclamations to summon and instruct them, gathering forces to await the arrival of the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shandong all wished to join him. Wei Sheng sent proclamations summoning them, gathering forces to await the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 沂民壁蒼山者數十萬，金人圍之，久不下，砦首滕{曰狄}告急於勝。

translations.literal: Several hundred thousand people of Yi who had fortified themselves on Cang Mountain were besieged by the Jurchens for a long time without falling; the stockade leader Teng Gao sent urgent word to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred thousand people of Yi who had fortified Cang Mountain were besieged by the Jin for a long time without falling. The stockade leader Teng Gao sent urgent word to Wei Sheng.

sentences.zh: 勝提兵往救之，陣於山下。

translations.literal: Sheng led troops to rescue them and drew up his line at the foot of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng led troops to the rescue and drew up his line at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 金人多伏兵，勝兵遇伏，皆赴砦。

translations.literal: The Jurchens had many ambushes; Sheng's troops met the ambush and all fled to the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had set many ambushes. Wei Sheng's troops met them and all fled to the stockade.

sentences.zh: 金人襲之，勝單騎而殿，以大刀奮擊。

translations.literal: The Jurchens struck them; Sheng alone on horseback brought up the rear and fought fiercely with a great blade.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin struck them. Wei Sheng alone on horseback brought up the rear and fought fiercely with a great blade.

sentences.zh: 金人望見勝，知其為將也，以五百騎圍之數重。

translations.literal: The Jurchens saw Sheng and knew he was the general; with five hundred horsemen they surrounded him in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin saw Wei Sheng and knew he was the commander. Five hundred horsemen surrounded him in ring after ring.

sentences.zh: 勝馳突四擊，金陣開復闔。

translations.literal: Sheng galloped and charged in four directions; the Jin line opened and closed again.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng galloped and charged in every direction. The Jin line opened and closed again around him.

sentences.zh: 戰移時，身被數十槍，冒刃出圍。

translations.literal: The battle lasted some time; his body took scores of spear wounds; he braved the blades and broke out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The battle lasted some time. He took scores of spear wounds but braved the blades and broke out of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 金兵追之，馬中矢踣，步而入砦，無敢當者。

translations.literal: Jin troops pursued him; his horse was struck by an arrow and fell; he entered the stockade on foot; no one dared stand in his way.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops pursued him. His horse was struck by an arrow and fell. He entered the stockade on foot, and no one dared stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 金人又急攻，絕其水，砦中食幹Я，殺牛馬飲血，勝默禱而雨驟作。

translations.literal: The Jurchens pressed the attack again and cut off their water; in the stockade they ate dried provisions, killed cattle and horses and drank their blood; Sheng prayed in silence and rain suddenly fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin pressed the attack again and cut off their water. Inside the stockade they ate dried provisions, killed cattle and horses and drank their blood. Wei Sheng prayed in silence, and rain suddenly fell.

sentences.zh: 金人攻盆急，周山為營，勝度其必復攻海州，因間出砦越城中。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked all the more urgently and encircled the mountain with camps; Sheng judged that they would certainly attack Haizhou again; he therefore stole out of the stockade by night and crossed through the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin attacked all the more urgently and encircled the mountain with camps. Wei Sheng judged that they would certainly attack Haizhou again. He stole out of the stockade by night and crossed through the city.

sentences.zh: 金人果解蒼山圍，自新橋抵城下，勝出戰皆捷。

translations.literal: The Jurchens indeed lifted the siege of Cangshan, came from Xinqiao to beneath the walls, and Sheng went out to fight with victory in every encounter.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin indeed lifted the siege of Cangshan, marched from Xinqiao to the foot of the walls, and Wei Sheng sallied forth to fight, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 金分兵四面攻之，勝募士登城以禦，矢石如雨者七日，金兵死傷多，遁去。

translations.literal: The Jin divided their forces to attack from all four sides. Sheng recruited men to mount the walls and defend. For seven days arrows and stones fell like rain. Many Jin soldiers were killed or wounded, and they fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin split their army and attacked from all four sides. Wei Sheng recruited men to man the walls in defense. For seven days arrows and stones rained down without cease. Many Jin soldiers were killed or wounded, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勝嘗出戰，矢中鼻貫齒，不能食，猶親禦戰。

translations.literal: Sheng once went out to battle. An arrow struck his nose and pierced through to his teeth. He could not eat, yet still personally commanded the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Wei Sheng went out to fight, an arrow struck his nose and pierced through to his teeth. He could not eat, yet he still commanded the battle in person.

sentences.zh: 勝起義久，朝廷尚未知。

translations.literal: Sheng had risen in rebellion for a long time, but the court did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng had been in rebellion for a long time, but the court still did not know of it.

sentences.zh: 沿海制置使李寶遣其子公佐由海道覘敵，至州，始遣忠義將朱震、褚道詣行在，白勝姓名於執政，始知勝之功焉。

translations.literal: The Coastal Military Commissioner Li Bao sent his son Gongzuo by sea to reconnoiter the enemy. When he reached the prefecture, he dispatched the loyalist generals Zhu Zhen and Chu Dao to the mobile court to report Sheng's name to the chief ministers, and only then did they learn of Sheng's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The Coastal Military Commissioner Li Bao sent his son Gongzuo by sea to scout the enemy. When he reached Haizhou, he dispatched the loyalist generals Zhu Zhen and Chu Dao to the mobile court to report Wei Sheng's name to the chief ministers, and only then did the court learn of his achievements.

sentences.zh: 金主亮舉兵渡淮，慮勝睨其後，分軍數萬來攻。

translations.literal: Emperor Liang of Jin raised troops and crossed the Huai. Fearing Sheng might threaten his rear, he divided several tens of thousands of men to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Liang raised an army and crossed the Huai River. Fearing that Wei Sheng might threaten his rear, he detached several tens of thousands of men to attack Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 會李寶帥舟師往膠西，破金人舟艦，勝遣人邀之，同擊金人於新橋，大敗之。

translations.literal: Just then Li Bao led his fleet to Jiaoxi and broke the Jurchen ships. Sheng sent men to invite him, and together they struck the Jurchens at Xinqiao and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Bao led his fleet to Jiaoxi and destroyed the Jin ships. Wei Sheng sent men to invite him, and together they attacked the Jin at Xinqiao and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 金兵未退，寶知金舟將遁，復以兵登舟備海道。

translations.literal: The Jin army had not yet withdrawn. Bao knew the Jin ships were about to flee, so again he put his men aboard to guard the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army had not yet withdrawn. Li Bao knew the Jin fleet was about to flee, so he again put his men aboard ship to guard the sea lanes.

sentences.zh: 金主初命造海艦，欲分軍入蘇、杭，悉以中原民操舟楫。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler had initially ordered sea vessels built, intending to send troops in separate columns into Suzhou and Hangzhou, with natives of the Central Plains entirely manning the boats.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ruler had earlier ordered sea vessels built, intending to send troops in separate columns into Suzhou and Hangzhou, with men from the Central Plains entirely crewing the boats.

sentences.zh: 民家送衣裘者相告語，俟王師至即背之。

translations.literal: Families delivering clothing and fur garments told one another they would turn against the Jin as soon as the imperial army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Families delivering clothing and furs told one another that they would turn against the Jin as soon as the imperial army arrived.

sentences.zh: 及寶舟入島中，適北風勁，舟不進。

translations.literal: When Bao's ships entered among the islands, a strong north wind was blowing and the vessels could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bao's ships entered the islands, a strong north wind was blowing and the fleet could not advance.

sentences.zh: 有頃反風，金人艤舟於岸，操舟者望見寶舟，謬雲此金國兵也，俾皆入舟中。

translations.literal: Before long the wind shifted. The Jurchens moored their boats at shore. The boatmen, seeing Bao's fleet, falsely said these were Jin troops and ordered everyone into the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the wind shifted. The Jin moored their boats along the shore. The boatmen, seeing Li Bao's fleet, falsely declared them to be Jin troops and ordered everyone back aboard.

sentences.zh: 舟忽至，金人不知，寶縱火焚其舟。

translations.literal: The ships suddenly arrived. The Jurchens did not know what was happening. Bao set fire and burned their vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The ships suddenly arrived. The Jin did not realize what was happening. Li Bao set fire and burned their vessels.

sentences.zh: 舟以赤油絹為帆，風順火熾，操舟者皆登岸走。

translations.literal: The ships had sails of red oiled silk. With the wind favorable, the fire blazed fiercely. The boatmen all scrambled ashore and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The ships had sails of red oiled silk. With the wind at their backs, the flames roared. The boatmen all scrambled ashore and fled.

sentences.zh: 金兵在舟中者，坐以待縛，載之檻車，悉獲其舟。

translations.literal: Jurchen soldiers still aboard sat waiting to be bound. They were loaded into caged carts, and all their ships were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Jin soldiers still aboard sat waiting to be bound. They were loaded into caged carts, and all their ships were captured.

sentences.zh: 寶既捷，勝亦還州為捍禦計。

translations.literal: After his victory, Bao [departed]; Sheng also returned to the prefecture to plan its defense.
translations.idiomatic: After his victory, Li Bao departed, and Wei Sheng also returned to Haizhou to plan its defense.

sentences.zh: 金兵至，營於城北砂巷，列陣將攻關門，先遣人說勝使降。

translations.literal: Jin troops arrived, encamped at Shaxiang north of the city, formed ranks to assault the pass gate, and first sent men to urge Sheng to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops arrived, encamped at Shaxiang north of the city, formed battle lines to assault the pass gate, and first sent envoys to urge Wei Sheng to surrender.

sentences.zh: 勝開門出諭之曰：「汝主叛盟失信，無故興兵，我朝以仁義之師，來復舊疆，汝主渡淮必敗。

translations.literal: Sheng opened the gate and came out to address them, saying: "Your ruler broke the alliance and betrayed trust, raising troops without cause. Our dynasty sends an army of benevolence and righteousness to recover our old territories. Your ruler will surely be defeated when he crosses the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng opened the gate and came out to address them, saying, "Your ruler broke the alliance and betrayed his word, raising troops without cause. Our dynasty sends an army of benevolence and righteousness to recover our old territories. Your ruler will surely be defeated when he crosses the Huai.

sentences.zh: 爾等宜早來歸，必獲爵賞。

translations.literal: You all should come over early and will surely receive ranks and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: You should come over to us early, and you will surely receive ranks and rewards.

sentences.zh: 」時金兵已逼關，勝登關門張樂飲酒，犒軍士，令固守勿出戰。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin army had already pressed close to the pass. Sheng mounted the pass gate, set out music and drank wine, rewarded the soldiers, and ordered them to hold firm and not go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Jin army had already pressed close to the pass. Wei Sheng mounted the pass gate, set out music and drank wine, rewarded his soldiers, and ordered them to hold firm and not sally forth.

sentences.zh: 金兵攻之逾時，乃少遣士出，憑險隘擊之。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked for a long while. Then he sent out only a few men to strike them from the narrow defile.
