translations.idiomatic: The Jin attacked for a long while. Then Wei Sheng sent out only a few men to strike them from the narrow defile.

sentences.zh: 金人知不可攻，率軍轉而渡河，襲關後。

translations.literal: The Jurchens realized the place could not be taken. They led their army to turn and cross the river, attacking behind the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin realized the position could not be taken. They led their army around to cross the river and attack from behind the pass.

sentences.zh: 勝斂兵入城，金兵追將及，勝獨乘馬逐之，叱曰：「魏勝在此！

translations.literal: Sheng drew in his troops and entered the city. Jin troops pursued, almost reaching him. Sheng alone rode a horse to chase them back, shouting: "Wei Sheng is here!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng drew in his troops and entered the city. Jin soldiers pursued, nearly catching up. He alone rode out after them, shouting, "Wei Sheng is here!

sentences.zh: 」聞之皆辟易，士卒後入者不復敢追。

translations.literal: Upon hearing this all shrank back. The soldiers who entered last no longer dared pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, they all shrank back. The soldiers who entered the city last no longer dared pursue.

sentences.zh: 勝軍已入城，金兵徑趨城東，欲過砂堰環城為營。

translations.literal: Sheng's army had entered the city. The Jin troops went straight toward the east of the city, intending to pass Shayan and encircle the city with their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng's army had entered the city. The Jin troops headed straight for the east side, intending to pass Shayan and encircle the city with their camp.

sentences.zh: 勝先已據堰備之，金軍不得過，拒戰竟日，終不能近。

translations.literal: Sheng had already seized the weir and prepared defenses. The Jin army could not pass. They fought at the barricade all day but ultimately could not draw near.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng had already seized the weir and prepared defenses. The Jin army could not get through. They fought at the barricade all day but ultimately could not draw near.

sentences.zh: 有新募士守河者，不知兵，金兵遽過河，勝恐絕河路，亟收軍入城。

translations.literal: Newly recruited men were guarding the river and did not understand warfare. The Jin troops suddenly crossed the river. Sheng feared his river route would be cut off and hastily withdrew his army into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Newly recruited men were guarding the river and did not understand warfare. The Jin suddenly crossed the river. Wei Sheng feared his river route would be cut off and hastily withdrew his army into the city.

sentences.zh: 金兵追至東門外黃土阪，勝單騎逐之，大叱之，金兵五百皆望風退。

translations.literal: Jin troops pursued to the Yellow Earth Slope outside the east gate. Sheng alone on horseback chased them, shouting fiercely. Five hundred Jin soldiers all fled at the sight of him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops pursued to the Yellow Earth Slope outside the east gate. Wei Sheng alone on horseback chased them, shouting fiercely. Five hundred Jin soldiers all fled at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 勝又追十數里，士得入城；

translations.literal: Sheng chased them another ten-odd li until the soldiers were able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng chased them another ten-odd li until his soldiers were able to enter the city.

sentences.zh: 有不得入者，由城南入西門。

translations.literal: Those who could not enter went in through the west gate from the south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not enter did so through the west gate from the south of the city.

sentences.zh: 金兵復自西南來襲，勝從後叱之，金兵駭散，手殺數人。

translations.literal: Jin troops again came to attack from the southwest. Sheng shouted from behind them. The Jin soldiers scattered in terror, and he personally killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops again attacked from the southwest. Wei Sheng shouted from behind them. The Jin soldiers scattered in terror, and he personally killed several men.

sentences.zh: 奏功授閣門祗候，差知海州兼山東路忠義軍都統。

translations.literal: His achievements were reported and he was appointed Gate Attendant, assigned as prefect of Haizhou and concurrently commander of the Shandong Loyalist Army.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were reported to the throne, and he was appointed Gate Attendant and assigned as prefect of Haizhou, concurrently serving as commander of the Shandong Loyalist Army.

sentences.zh: 遣其子昌同峒峿山首領張榮，持旗榜往結山東忠義。

translations.literal: He sent his son Chang together with Zhang Rong, chieftain of Dongmou Mountain, bearing flags and proclamations to rally the Shandong loyalists.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Chang together with Zhang Rong, chieftain of Dongmou Mountain, bearing flags and proclamations to rally the Shandong loyalists.

sentences.zh: 金兵自新橋、關子門、砂堰之敗，殺傷者眾。

translations.literal: From their defeats at Xinqiao, Guanzimen, and Shayan, many Jin soldiers had been killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: From their defeats at Xinqiao, Guanzimen, and Shayan, many Jin soldiers had been killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 一日黎明，乘昏霧，四面薄城急攻。

translations.literal: One day at dawn, taking advantage of thick mist, they pressed in from all sides and attacked the city urgently.
translations.idiomatic: One day at dawn, taking advantage of thick mist, they pressed in from all sides and launched a fierce assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 勝激厲士卒，竭力捍禦，矢石交下。

translations.literal: Sheng roused his soldiers and defended with all their strength as arrows and stones rained down from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng roused his soldiers and defended with all their strength as arrows and stones rained down from both sides.

sentences.zh: 城上鎔金液，投火牛。

translations.literal: From atop the walls they poured molten metal and hurled fire oxen.
translations.idiomatic: From atop the walls they poured molten metal and hurled fire oxen.

sentences.zh: 金兵不能前，多死傷，乃拔砦走。

translations.literal: Jin troops could not advance. Many were killed or wounded, and they then broke camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin could not advance. Many were killed or wounded, and they then broke camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 距海州為長垣，包州城於中，使不能出。

translations.literal: They built a long wall around Haizhou, enclosing the prefectural city within, so that no one could get out.
translations.idiomatic: They built a long wall around Haizhou, enclosing the prefectural city within so that no one could get out.

sentences.zh: 及亮死，乃解去。

translations.literal: When Liang died, they finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanyan Liang died, they finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 勝善用大刀，能左右射，旗揭曰「山東魏勝」，金人望見即退走。

translations.literal: Sheng was skilled with the broadsword and could shoot to left and right. His banner read "Wei Sheng of Shandong." When the Jurchens saw it they immediately retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng was skilled with the broadsword and could shoot to left and right. His banner read "Wei Sheng of Shandong." When the Jin saw it they immediately retreated.

sentences.zh: 勝為旗十數，書其姓名，密付諸將，遇鏖戰即揭之，金兵悉避走。

translations.literal: Sheng made more than ten banners inscribed with his name and secretly gave them to his generals. Whenever fierce battle occurred they would raise them, and Jin soldiers all avoided and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng made more than ten banners inscribed with his name and secretly gave them to his generals. Whenever fierce fighting broke out they would raise them, and Jin soldiers all avoided and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，勝起義時，無州郡糧餉之給，無府庫倉廩之儲。

translations.literal: At first when Sheng rose in rebellion, there was no provision of grain and pay from prefectures and districts, and no stores in government treasuries and granaries.
translations.idiomatic: At first when Wei Sheng rose in rebellion, there was no grain or pay from the prefectures and districts, and no stores in government treasuries or granaries.

sentences.zh: 勝經畫市易，課酒榷鹽，勸糶豪右。

translations.literal: Sheng organized market trade, levied taxes on wine and monopolized salt, and encouraged wealthy landowners to sell grain.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng organized market trade, levied taxes on wine and monopolized salt, and encouraged wealthy landowners to sell grain.

sentences.zh: 環海州度視敵兵攻取處，築城浚隍，塞關隘，在軍，未嘗一日懈弛，恒如寇至。

translations.literal: All around Haizhou he surveyed where enemy troops might attack, built walls and dug moats, and blocked passes. While with the army he never relaxed for a single day, always as if invaders were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: All around Haizhou he surveyed where enemy troops might attack, built walls and dug moats, and blocked the passes. While with the army he never relaxed for a single day, always as if invaders were about to arrive.

sentences.zh: 方糾集遠邇，犒勞士卒，期約有日，會金主亮被弑，金兵北歸，王師亦南還矣。

translations.literal: Just as he was gathering men from near and far and preparing to reward the soldiers on a set day, Emperor Liang of Jin was assassinated. Jin troops returned north, and the imperial army also withdrew south.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was gathering men from near and far and preparing to reward the soldiers on a set day, Wanyan Liang was assassinated. Jin troops returned north, and the imperial army also withdrew south.

sentences.zh: 初，亮聞勝在海州，知不可取，曰：「少須，他時取之易耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liang heard Sheng was at Haizhou and knew it could not be taken, he said: "Wait a little; it will be easy to take another time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wanyan Liang heard that Wei Sheng was at Haizhou and knew it could not be taken, he said, "Wait a little; it will be easy to take another time.

sentences.zh: 」亮既殞，勝益得自治軍旅，人皆精銳。

translations.literal: After Liang died, Sheng was all the more able to manage his own army. Every man was elite and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang died, Wei Sheng was all the more able to manage his own army. Every man was elite and sharp.

sentences.zh: 獲金諜者，犒以酒食，厚賂遣還。

translations.literal: When he captured Jin spies, he treated them with wine and food, gave them generous gifts, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: When he captured Jin spies, he treated them with wine and food, gave them generous gifts, and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 有自北方來歸者，與之同臥起，共飲食，示以不疑；

translations.literal: When men came over from the north to defect, he slept and rose with them, ate and drank together, showing that he harbored no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When men came over from the north to defect, he slept and rose with them, ate and drank together, showing that he harbored no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 周其窶貧，使之感激。

translations.literal: He attended to their poverty and hardship, moving them to gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: He attended to their poverty and hardship, moving them to gratitude.

sentences.zh: 自是山東、河北歸附者眾，得金人虛實，悉以上聞。

translations.literal: From then on many from Shandong and Hebei came to join him. Whatever intelligence they obtained on Jin strength and disposition, he reported entirely to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: From then on many from Shandong and Hebei came to join him. Whatever intelligence they obtained on Jin strength and disposition, he reported entirely to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又第其忠義士功能，假授官資，因李寶轉達於朝，悉如所請。

translations.literal: He also ranked his loyalists by merit and provisionally granted them official titles and stipends. Through Li Bao he forwarded these to the court, and all were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: He also ranked his loyalists by merit and provisionally granted them official titles and stipends. Through Li Bao he forwarded these to the court, and all were granted as requested.

sentences.zh: 金人遣山東路都統、總管以兵十萬攻海州。

translations.literal: The Jurchens sent the Shandong circuit commander-in-chief and grand commander with an army of one hundred thousand to attack Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent the Shandong circuit commander-in-chief and grand commander with an army of one hundred thousand to attack Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 時寶帥海舟水陸並進，抵城北砂巷，勝率眾合寶軍大破之，斬首不可計，堰水為之不流，餘悉奔潰。

translations.literal: At the time Bao led his sea fleet advancing by land and water together, reaching Shaxiang north of the city. Sheng led the masses to join Bao's army and inflicted a great defeat. Heads cut off were beyond counting. The weir water was choked so it would not flow. The rest all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Bao led his sea fleet advancing by land and water together, reaching Shaxiang north of the city. Wei Sheng led his forces to join Li Bao's army and inflicted a great defeat. Heads cut off were beyond counting. The weir water was choked so it would not flow. The rest all fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 勝獨率兵追北二十里，至新橋，又破之，盡獲其鞍馬器甲。

translations.literal: Sheng alone led troops pursuing the fleeing enemy twenty li to Xinqiao, defeating them again and capturing all their saddles, horses, armor, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng alone led troops pursuing the fleeing enemy twenty li to Xinqiao, defeating them again and capturing all their saddles, horses, armor, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 寶亦駐海州，為進取計。

translations.literal: Bao also stationed himself at Haizhou to plan advances.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao also stationed himself at Haizhou to plan further advances.

sentences.zh: 金人復遣五斤太師發諸路兵二十余萬來攻海州，先遣一軍自州西南斷勝軍餉道。

translations.literal: The Jurchens again sent Grand Preceptor Wujin to mobilize more than two hundred thousand troops from all routes to attack Haizhou. They first dispatched one army from the southwest of the prefecture to cut Sheng's supply line.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin again sent Grand Preceptor Wujin to mobilize more than two hundred thousand troops from all routes to attack Haizhou. They first dispatched one army from the southwest of the prefecture to cut Wei Sheng's supply line.

sentences.zh: 勝驛勇悍士三千餘騎，拒于石闥堰，金軍不能進。

translations.literal: Sheng selected more than three thousand fierce riders and blocked them at the Shitie Weir. The Jin army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng selected more than three thousand fierce riders and blocked them at the Shitie Weir. The Jin army could not advance.

sentences.zh: 逮夜始還，留千人備險隘。

translations.literal: He returned only at nightfall, leaving one thousand men to guard the narrow passes.
translations.idiomatic: He returned only at nightfall, leaving one thousand men to guard the narrow passes.

sentences.zh: 金兵十萬來奪，勝率眾鏖戰，殺數千人，餘皆遁去，下令守險勿追。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand Jin troops came to seize the position. Sheng led the masses in fierce battle, killing several thousand. The rest all fled. He ordered those guarding the passes not to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred thousand Jin troops came to seize the position. Wei Sheng led his forces in fierce battle, killing several thousand. The rest all fled. He ordered those guarding the passes not to pursue.

sentences.zh: 報寶，寶以防海道，登舟，不復發兵。

translations.literal: He reported to Bao. Bao, to guard the sea routes, went aboard his ships and no longer sent out troops.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Li Bao. Li Bao, to guard the sea routes, went aboard his ships and no longer sent out troops.

sentences.zh: 金兵盛集，勝力拒之，自旦至暮，金兵不能奪。

translations.literal: Jin troops massed in great numbers. Sheng resisted with all his strength from dawn until dusk. The Jin could not seize the position.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops massed in great numbers. Wei Sheng resisted with all his strength from dawn until dusk. The Jin could not seize the position.

sentences.zh: 勝令步卒整隊前行，自為殿。

translations.literal: Sheng ordered the infantry to march in formation ahead while he himself served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng ordered the infantry to march in formation ahead while he himself served as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 時百姓以寶既登舟，懼金兵大至，皆欲入城，統制郭蔚閉城門不納。

translations.literal: At the time the people, seeing that Bao had already boarded ship, feared great Jin forces were coming and all wanted to enter the city. The regimental commander Guo Wei closed the city gates and would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the people, seeing that Li Bao had already boarded ship, feared that great Jin forces were coming and all wanted to enter the city. The regimental commander Guo Wei closed the city gates and would not admit them.

sentences.zh: 人民牛馬蔽野，呼號動地，城中亦懼。

translations.literal: People and cattle and horses covered the fields. Their cries shook the earth. Inside the city there was fear as well.
translations.idiomatic: People, cattle, and horses covered the fields. Their cries shook the earth. Inside the city there was fear as well.

sentences.zh: 勝入城，諭以賊勢退怯之狀，固守可保無虞，乃開門盡納之。

translations.literal: Sheng entered the city and told them the enemy was in retreat and growing timid, that holding firm could ensure safety. He then opened the gates and admitted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng entered the city and told them the enemy was in retreat and growing timid, that holding firm could ensure their safety. He then opened the gates and admitted them all.

sentences.zh: 居無何，金兵環城圍數重，勝與郭蔚分兵備禦，偃旗僕鼓，寂若無人。

translations.literal: Before long, Jin troops encircled the city in many rings. Sheng and Guo Wei divided forces to defend, lowered flags and muffled drums, silent as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Jin troops encircled the city in many rings. Wei Sheng and Guo Wei divided their forces to defend, lowered flags and muffled drums, silent as if no one were there.

sentences.zh: 金軍驚疑，數日不敢攻，已乃植雲梯，置炮石，四面合圍，負土填壕。

translations.literal: The Jin army was alarmed and suspicious. For several days they dared not attack. Then they erected cloud ladders, emplaced catapults and stones, closed in from all four sides, and carried earth to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army was alarmed and suspicious. For several days they dared not attack. Then they erected cloud ladders, emplaced catapults and stones, closed in from all four sides, and carried earth to fill the moat.

sentences.zh: 勝俟其近城，鳴鼓張旗，矢石俱發，繼以火牛、金液，凡三晝夜，金兵竟不能近。

translations.literal: Sheng waited until they drew near the walls, then sounded drums and raised flags. Arrows and stones flew together, followed by fire oxen and molten metal. For three days and nights the Jin ultimately could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng waited until they drew near the walls, then sounded drums and raised flags. Arrows and stones flew together, followed by fire oxen and molten metal. For three days and nights the Jin ultimately could not approach.

sentences.zh: 於是罷攻，修營壘，絕河道，謀為固守。

translations.literal: Thereupon they ceased the assault, repaired fortifications, cut off the river channels, and planned to hold firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they ceased the assault, repaired fortifications, cut off the river channels, and planned to hold firmly.

sentences.zh: 勝俟其不備掩擊，或獨出擾之，使不得休息。

translations.literal: Sheng waited for them unprepared and struck by surprise, or went out alone to harass them so they could not rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng waited for them unprepared and struck by surprise, or went out alone to harass them so they could not rest.

sentences.zh: 又間夜發兵劫其營，或焚其攻具。

translations.literal: He also sent troops by night at intervals to raid their camps or burn their siege equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent troops by night at intervals to raid their camps or burn their siege equipment.

sentences.zh: 既而金人並力急攻，勝告急于李寶。

translations.literal: Before long the Jurchens combined their strength in a fierce assault. Sheng urgently informed Li Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jin combined their strength in a fierce assault. Wei Sheng urgently informed Li Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶以聞，還報城中，已命張子蓋率兵來解圍。

translations.literal: Bao reported upward and sent word back to the city that he had already ordered Zhang Zigai to lead troops to relieve the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bao reported upward and sent word back to the city that he had already ordered Zhang Zigai to lead troops to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 金人亦知子蓋軍且至，已有退意。

translations.literal: The Jurchens also knew Zigai's army was about to arrive and already had thoughts of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin also knew that Zhang Zigai's army was about to arrive and already had thoughts of retreat.

sentences.zh: 頃之，子蓋先帥騎兵至，勝出與子蓋議戰事，且促其步卒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Zigai arrived first leading cavalry. Sheng went out to discuss military affairs with Zigai and also urged on his infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Zhang Zigai arrived first leading cavalry. Wei Sheng went out to discuss military affairs with him and also urged on his infantry.

sentences.zh: 勝出軍城北砂巷，與金軍大戰，斬首不可計，追數十里，餘兵皆遁。

translations.literal: Sheng led his army out at Shaxiang north of the city, fought a great battle with the Jin army, cut off heads beyond counting, pursued for several tens of li, and the remaining troops all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng led his army out at Shaxiang north of the city, fought a great battle with the Jin army, cut off heads beyond counting, pursued for several tens of li, and the remaining troops all fled.

sentences.zh: 勝與子蓋議進討，子蓋曰：「受詔解圍，不知其他。

translations.literal: Sheng discussed advancing to attack further with Zigai. Zigai said: "I received orders to relieve the siege. I know nothing beyond that.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng discussed advancing to attack further with Zhang Zigai. Zhang said, "I received orders to relieve the siege. I know nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 」遂率軍還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he led his army back.

sentences.zh: 城中疑懼，欲隨王師出，勝親邀於道而諭之，至漣水軍，與偕還。

translations.literal: Inside the city people were anxious and afraid, wanting to leave with the imperial army. Sheng personally intercepted them on the road and persuaded them. At Lianshui Army camp he went back together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city people were anxious and afraid, wanting to leave with the imperial army. Wei Sheng personally intercepted them on the road and persuaded them. At Lianshui Army camp he went back together with them.

sentences.zh: 時都督張浚在建康，招勝，詢以軍務。

translations.literal: At the time the overall commander Zhang Jun was at Jiankang. He summoned Sheng and inquired about military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the overall commander Zhang Jun was at Jiankang. He summoned Wei Sheng and inquired about military affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉閣門宣贊舍人，差充山東路忠義軍都統制兼鎮江府駐劄御前前軍統制，仍知海州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gate Proclamation Attendant, assigned as commander of the Shandong Loyalist Army and concurrently commander of the forward army stationed at Zhenjiang Prefecture under the imperial direct command, while still serving as prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gate Proclamation Attendant, assigned as commander of the Shandong Loyalist Army and concurrently commander of the forward army stationed at Zhenjiang Prefecture under the imperial direct command, while still serving as prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 勝還。

translations.literal: Sheng returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng returned.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，詔以鎮江御前同統制魏全來守海州，督府亦遣賈和仲充山東、河北路招撫使，節制本路軍馬，海州駐劄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, an edict appointed Wei Quan, co-commander of the Zhenjiang imperial direct forces, to garrison Haizhou. The headquarters also dispatched Jia Hezhong as commissioner for pacifying Shandong and Hebei routes, controlling the troops of those circuits, stationed at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing, an edict appointed Wei Quan, co-commander of the Zhenjiang imperial direct forces, to garrison Haizhou. The headquarters also dispatched Jia Hezhong as commissioner for pacifying Shandong and Hebei routes, controlling the troops of those circuits, stationed at Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 和仲忌勝，陰誘忠義軍使不安。

translations.literal: Hezhong envied Sheng and secretly incited the loyalist army to feel insecure.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hezhong envied Wei Sheng and secretly incited the loyalist army to feel insecure.

sentences.zh: 勝與辨是非，和仲又讒勝於都督，惑之。

translations.literal: Sheng debated right and wrong with him. Hezhong also slandered Sheng to the overall commander, confusing him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng debated right and wrong with him. Hezhong also slandered Wei Sheng to the overall commander, confusing him.

sentences.zh: 呼勝至鎮江計事，罷其職，改京東路馬步軍副總管、都督府統制，建康府駐劄。

translations.literal: He summoned Sheng to Zhenjiang to discuss affairs, dismissed him from his post, and changed his appointment to deputy grand commander of cavalry and infantry on the Jingdong route and headquarters regimental commander, stationed at Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Wei Sheng to Zhenjiang to discuss affairs, dismissed him from his post, and changed his appointment to deputy grand commander of cavalry and infantry on the Jingdong route and headquarters regimental commander, stationed at Jiankang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既而督府知和仲所誣，罷之，復勝舊職，仍遣鎮江御前後軍屯海州，代前軍還鎮江。

translations.literal: Later the headquarters learned Hezhong's accusations were false. They dismissed him, restored Sheng to his former post, and still sent the rear army of the Zhenjiang imperial direct forces to garrison Haizhou, replacing the forward army which returned to Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later the headquarters learned that Hezhong's accusations were false. They dismissed him, restored Wei Sheng to his former post, and still sent the rear army of the Zhenjiang imperial direct forces to garrison Haizhou, replacing the forward army which returned to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 勝既還海州，鎮撫一方，民安其政。

translations.literal: Once Sheng returned to Haizhou, he pacified the region. The people were secure under his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei Sheng returned to Haizhou, he pacified the region. The people were secure under his governance.

sentences.zh: 改忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 海州城西南枕孤山，敵至，登山瞰城中，虛實立見，故西南受敵最劇。

translations.literal: Haizhou city's southwest rested against Lone Mountain. When enemies arrived they mounted the hill and overlooked the city; strength and weakness were immediately visible. Thus the southwest bore the heaviest enemy pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhou city's southwest rested against Lone Mountain. When enemies arrived they mounted the hill and overlooked the city; strength and weakness were immediately visible. Thus the southwest bore the heaviest enemy pressure.

sentences.zh: 勝築重城，圍山在內，寇至則先據之，不能害。

translations.literal: Sheng built an outer wall enclosing the mountain within. When invaders came he first seized it, and they could do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng built an outer wall enclosing the mountain within. When invaders came he first seized it, and they could do no harm.

sentences.zh: 勝嘗自創如意戰車數百兩，炮車數十兩，車上為獸面木牌，大槍數十，垂氈幕軟牌，每車用二人推轂，可蔽五十人。

translations.literal: Sheng once on his own devised several hundred Ruyi war chariots and several dozen cannon chariots. On each chariot were beast-faced wooden shields, several dozen long spears, hanging felt curtains and soft shields. Each chariot used two men to push the wheels and could shelter fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng once on his own devised several hundred Ruyi war chariots and several dozen cannon chariots. On each chariot were beast-faced wooden shields, several dozen long spears, hanging felt curtains and soft shields. Each chariot used two men to push the wheels and could shelter fifty men.

sentences.zh: 行則載輜重器甲，止則為營，掛搭如城壘，人馬不能近；

translations.literal: When moving they carried baggage, weapons, and armor. When halted they formed camps, rigged up like walled fortifications that men and horses could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: When moving they carried baggage, weapons, and armor. When halted they formed camps, rigged up like walled fortifications that men and horses could not approach.

sentences.zh: 遇敵又可以禦箭簇。

translations.literal: When encountering the enemy they could also shield against volleys of arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When encountering the enemy they could also shield against volleys of arrows.

sentences.zh: 列陣則如意車在外，以旗蔽障，弩車當陣門，其上置床子弩，矢大如鑿，一矢能射數人，發三矢可數百步。

translations.literal: When forming battle arrays the Ruyi chariots were placed outside with flags as screens. Crossbow chariots stood at the array gates, mounting bed crossbows whose bolts were as large as chisels—one bolt could strike several men, and three shots could reach several hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: When forming battle arrays the Ruyi chariots were placed outside with flags as screens. Crossbow chariots stood at the array gates, mounting bed crossbows whose bolts were as large as chisels—one bolt could strike several men, and three shots could reach several hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 炮車在陣中，施火石炮，亦二百步。

translations.literal: Cannon chariots were in the center of the array, firing fire-stone cannons, also effective to two hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: Cannon chariots were in the center of the array, firing fire-stone cannons, also effective to two hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 兩陣相近，則陣間發弓弩箭炮，近陣門則刀斧槍手突出，交陣則出騎兵，兩響掩擊，得捷拔陣追襲，少卻則入陣間稍憩。

translations.literal: When the two arrays drew near, bows, crossbows, arrows, and cannon fired from within the formation. Near the array gates sword, axe, and spear men burst forth. When arrays clashed cavalry sallied out. At two signals they struck under cover. Gaining victory they broke formation to pursue. If they fell back slightly they withdrew into the formation to rest briefly.
translations.idiomatic: When the two arrays drew near, bows, crossbows, arrows, and cannon fired from within the formation. Near the array gates sword, axe, and spear men burst forth. When the arrays clashed cavalry sallied out. At two signals they struck under cover. Gaining victory they broke formation to pursue. If they fell back slightly they withdrew into the formation to rest briefly.

sentences.zh: 士卒不疲，進退俱利。

translations.literal: The soldiers did not grow weary; advance and retreat were both advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers did not grow weary; advance and retreat were both advantageous.

sentences.zh: 伺便出擊，慮有拒遏，預為解脫計，夜習不使人見。

translations.literal: When they saw an opportunity they sallied forth to attack; fearing they might be blocked and held back, he prepared escape plans in advance, practicing at night without letting others see.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw an opportunity they sallied forth to attack; fearing they might be blocked and cut off, he prepared escape plans in advance, drilling at night where no one could see.

sentences.zh: 以其制上於朝，詔諸軍遵其式造焉。

translations.literal: He submitted his design to the court, and an edict ordered all armies to follow his model in making them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted his design to the court, and an edict ordered every army to follow his model in building them.

sentences.zh: 二年，以議和撤海州戍，命勝知楚州，以本州官吏及部兵赴新治。

translations.literal: In the second year, because of the peace negotiations the Haizhou garrison was withdrawn. Sheng was ordered to serve as prefect of Chuzhou, taking that prefecture's officials and his troops to the new seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, because of the peace negotiations the Haizhou garrison was withdrawn. Wei Sheng was ordered to serve as prefect of Chuzhou, taking that prefecture's officials and his troops to the new administrative seat.

sentences.zh: 詔勝同淮東路安撫使劉寶、知高郵軍劉敏措置盱眙軍、楚州一帶，勝專一措置清河口。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sheng, together with Huaidong Circuit pacification commissioner Liu Bao and Gaoyou prefect Liu Min, to arrange defenses for the Xuyi and Chuzhou region; Sheng alone was to arrange Qinghe River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wei Sheng, together with Huaidong Circuit pacification commissioner Liu Bao and Gaoyou prefect Liu Min, to arrange defenses for the Xuyi and Chuzhou region, while Wei Sheng alone was responsible for the Qinghe River mouth.

sentences.zh: 時和議尚未決，金兵乘其懈，以舟載器甲糗糧自清河出，欲侵邊。

translations.literal: At that time the peace agreement had not yet been settled. Jin troops took advantage of their laxity, loading armor, weapons, and rations onto boats and coming out through Qinghe River, intending to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the peace agreement had not yet been settled. Jin troops took advantage of their laxity, loading armor, weapons, and rations onto boats and coming out through the Qinghe River, intending to raid the border.

sentences.zh: 勝覘知之，身帥忠義士拒于清河口。

translations.literal: Sheng learned of this through reconnaissance and personally led loyalist volunteers to block them at Qinghe River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng learned of this through reconnaissance and personally led loyalist volunteers to block them at the Qinghe River mouth.

sentences.zh: 金兵詐稱欲運糧往泗州，由清河口入淮。

translations.literal: The Jin troops falsely claimed they wished to transport grain to Sizhou, entering the Huai via Qinghe River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin troops falsely claimed they wished to transport grain to Sizhou, entering the Huai River via the Qinghe River mouth.

sentences.zh: 勝知其謀，欲禦之，都統制劉寶以方議和，不許。

translations.literal: Sheng understood their scheme and wished to repel them, but commander-in-chief Liu Bao, citing the ongoing peace talks, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng understood their scheme and wished to repel them, but commander-in-chief Liu Bao, citing the ongoing peace talks, would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 金騎軼境，勝率諸軍拒于淮陽，自卯至申，勝負未決。

translations.literal: Jin cavalry raided across the border. Sheng led his various armies to resist at Huaiyang. From the mao hour to the shen hour, victory and defeat remained undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Jin cavalry raided across the border. Wei Sheng led his various armies to resist at Huaiyang. From the mao hour to the shen hour, victory and defeat remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 金軍增生兵來，勝與之力戰，又遣人告急於寶。

translations.literal: The Jin army brought up reinforcements. Sheng fought them fiercely and also sent men to urgently report to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army brought up reinforcements. Wei Sheng fought them fiercely and also sent men to urgently report to Liu Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶在楚州，相距四十里，堅謂方講和，決無戰事，迄不發一兵。

translations.literal: Bao was at Chuzhou, forty li away. He firmly maintained that peace was being negotiated and there would definitely be no fighting, and to the end did not send a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bao was at Chuzhou, forty li away. He firmly maintained that peace was being negotiated and there would definitely be no fighting, and to the end did not send a single soldier.

sentences.zh: 勝矢盡，救不至，猶依士阜為陣，謂士卒曰：「我當死此，得脫者歸報天子。

translations.literal: Sheng exhausted his arrows and relief did not arrive. He still formed battle lines on an earthen mound and told his soldiers: "I shall die here. Those who can escape should return and report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng exhausted his arrows and relief did not arrive. He still formed battle lines on an earthen mound and told his soldiers, "I shall die here. Those who can escape should return and report to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」乃令步卒居前，騎為殿，至淮陰東十八里，中矢，墜馬死，年四十五。

translations.literal: He then ordered the infantry to take the front and the cavalry to bring up the rear. Eighteen li east of Huaiyin he was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and died. He was forty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the infantry to take the front and the cavalry to bring up the rear. Eighteen li east of Huaiyin he was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and died at the age of forty-five.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈保甯軍節度使，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously awarded the title of military commissioner of Baoning Army and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously awarded the title of military commissioner of Baoning Army and given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Valiant).

sentences.zh: 時淮南未平，詔于鎮江府江口鎮立廟，賜號褒忠，仍俟事定更祠于戰沒處。

translations.literal: At that time Huainan was not yet pacified. An edict ordered a temple established at Jiangkou town in Zhenjiang prefecture, bestowing the title Honoring Loyalty, and further decreed that once affairs were settled worship would be moved to the place where he fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huainan was not yet pacified. An edict ordered a temple established at Jiangkou town in Zhenjiang prefecture, bestowing the title Honoring Loyalty, and further decreed that once affairs were settled worship would be moved to the place where he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 且令有司刻木以斂，葬於鎮江。

translations.literal: Moreover, officials were ordered to carve a wooden effigy for his interment, and he was buried at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, officials were ordered to carve a wooden effigy for his interment, and he was buried at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 官其二子，郊武功大夫、忠州刺史，昌承信郎。

translations.literal: His two sons were given official appointments: Jiao as Defender-in-Chief of Martial Achievement and prefect of Zhongzhou; Chang as Gentleman for Fidelity and Trust.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons were given official appointments: Jiao as Defender-in-Chief of Martial Achievement and prefect of Zhongzhou, and Chang as Gentleman for Fidelity and Trust.

sentences.zh: 賜銀千兩，絹千匹，宅一區，田百頃。

translations.literal: There were granted one thousand taels of silver, one thousand bolts of silk, one residence, and one hundred qing of farmland.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted one thousand taels of silver, one thousand bolts of silk, one residence, and one hundred qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 其後使者過淮東，始得其詳，還言於朝。

translations.literal: Later an envoy passing through eastern Huai obtained the full details and reported them upon returning to court.
translations.idiomatic: Later an envoy passing through eastern Huai obtained the full details and reported them upon returning to court.

sentences.zh: 以劉寶不出救兵，削兩鎮節鉞，沒入家貲，貶瓊州死。

translations.literal: Because Liu Bao had failed to send relief troops, his posts as commissioner of two circuits were stripped, his family assets confiscated, and he was demoted and sent to Qiongzhou, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Bao had failed to send relief troops, his posts as commissioner of two circuits were stripped, his family assets confiscated, and he was demoted and sent to Qiongzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 勝所糾集忠義，有為賈和仲誘隸別屯及撤戍隔絕者，尚五千餘人，入京口屯駐前軍。

translations.literal: The loyalist volunteers Sheng had gathered—some of whom had been induced by Jia Hezhong to serve in separate encampments and cut off by the withdrawal of garrisons—still numbered more than five thousand. They entered Jingkou and were stationed as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist volunteers Wei Sheng had gathered—some of whom had been induced by Jia Hezhong to serve in separate encampments and cut off by the withdrawal of garrisons—still numbered more than five thousand. They entered Jingkou and were stationed as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 郊，添差揚州兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: Jiao was given an additional assignment as superintendent of Yangzhou horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao was given an additional assignment as superintendent of Yangzhou horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十五年，孝宗語樞臣曰：「魏勝之子，當與優異。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chunxi, Xiaozong said to the privy councilors: "Wei Sheng's son should receive exceptional treatment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Chunxi, Emperor Xiaozong said to the privy councilors, "Wei Sheng's son should receive exceptional treatment.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「人材須用而後見，使魏勝不因邊釁，何以見其才？

translations.literal: He also said: "Talent must be employed before it can be seen. If Wei Sheng had not had a border crisis, how would his talent have been revealed?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Talent must be employed before it can be seen. If Wei Sheng had not faced a border crisis, how would his talent ever have been revealed?

sentences.zh: 」詔郊添差兩浙西路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jiao given an additional assignment as deputy commander of the horse and foot forces of western Zhejiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jiao given an additional assignment as deputy commander of the horse and foot forces of western Zhejiang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 張憲，飛愛將也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xian was Yue Fei's beloved general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian was Yue Fei's beloved general.

sentences.zh: 飛破曹成，憲與徐慶、王貴招降其党二萬。

translations.literal: When Yue Fei defeated Cao Cheng, Xian together with Xu Qing and Wang Gui induced twenty thousand of Cheng's followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei defeated Cao Cheng, Zhang Xian together with Xu Qing and Wang Gui induced twenty thousand of Cheng's followers to surrender.

sentences.zh: 有郝政率眾走沅州，首被白布，為成報仇，號「白巾賊」，憲一鼓擒之。

translations.literal: One Hao Zheng led his band to flee toward Yuanzhou. With white cloth on their heads, seeking revenge for Cheng, they were called the White-Turban Bandits. Xian captured them at the first drum roll.
translations.idiomatic: One Hao Zheng led his band to flee toward Yuanzhou. With white cloth on their heads, seeking revenge for Cao Cheng, they were called the White-Turban Bandits. Zhang Xian captured them at the first drum roll.

sentences.zh: 飛遣憲復隨州，敵將王嵩不戰而遁。

translations.literal: Yue Fei sent Xian to recover Suizhou. The enemy general Wang Song fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent Zhang Xian to recover Suizhou. The enemy general Wang Song fled without fighting.

sentences.zh: 進兵鄧州，距城三十里，遇賊兵數萬迎戰。

translations.literal: Advancing on Dengzhou, thirty li from the city they encountered tens of thousands of bandits coming out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Dengzhou, thirty li from the city they encountered tens of thousands of bandits coming out to fight.

sentences.zh: 與王萬、董先各出騎突擊，賊眾大潰，遂復鄧州。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Wan and Dong Xian, each led cavalry in a sudden assault. The bandit horde was utterly routed, and they recovered Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Wan and Dong Xian, each led cavalry in a sudden assault. The bandit horde was utterly routed, and they recovered Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，金人渝盟入侵，憲戰潁昌、戰陳州皆大捷，復其城。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Jin broke the treaty and invaded. Xian fought great victories at Yingchang and Chenzhou, recovering those cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the Jin broke the treaty and invaded. Zhang Xian won great victories at Yingchang and Chenzhou, recovering those cities.

sentences.zh: 兀朮頓兵十二萬於臨潁縣，楊再興與戰，死之。

translations.literal: Wuzhu massed one hundred twenty thousand troops at Linying county. Yang Zaixing fought him and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu massed one hundred twenty thousand troops at Linying county. Yang Zaixing fought him and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 憲繼至，破其潰兵八千，兀朮夜遁。

translations.literal: Xian arrived afterward, defeated eight thousand of their routed soldiers, and Wuzhu fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian arrived afterward, defeated eight thousand of their routed soldiers, and Wuzhu fled by night.

sentences.zh: 憲將徐慶、李山復捷于臨潁東北，破其眾六千，獲馬百匹，追奔十五里，中原大震。

translations.literal: Xian's subordinates Xu Qing and Li Shan won another victory northeast of Linying, defeating six thousand of the enemy, capturing one hundred horses, and pursuing the fleeing enemy fifteen li. The Central Plain was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian's subordinates Xu Qing and Li Shan won another victory northeast of Linying, defeating six thousand of the enemy, capturing one hundred horses, and pursuing the fleeing enemy fifteen li. The Central Plain was greatly shaken.

sentences.zh: 會秦檜主和，命飛班師，憲亦還。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui advocated peace, an order came for Yue Fei to withdraw his army, and Xian also returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui advocated peace, an order came for Yue Fei to withdraw his army, and Zhang Xian also returned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檜與張俊謀殺飛，密誘飛部曲，以能告飛事者，寵以優賞，卒無人應。

translations.literal: Before long, Qin Hui and Zhang Jun plotted to kill Yue Fei. They secretly tried to entice Yue Fei's officers and men, promising lavish rewards to anyone who could inform on Yue Fei's affairs. In the end no one responded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Qin Hui and Zhang Jun plotted to kill Yue Fei. They secretly tried to entice Yue Fei's officers and men, promising lavish rewards to anyone who could inform on Yue Fei's affairs. In the end no one responded.

sentences.zh: 聞飛嘗欲斬王貴，又杖之，誘貴告飛。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yue Fei had once wished to execute Wang Gui and had also beaten him, they tried to induce Gui to inform against Yue Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Yue Fei had once wished to execute Wang Gui and had also beaten him, they tried to induce Wang Gui to inform against Yue Fei.

sentences.zh: 貴不肯，曰：「為大將甯免以賞罰用人，苟以為怨，將不勝其怨。

translations.literal: Gui refused, saying: "As a great general one cannot avoid using reward and punishment to command men. If one resents this, a general cannot bear all such resentments.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui refused, saying, "As a great general one cannot avoid using reward and punishment to command men. If one resents this, a general cannot bear all such resentments.

sentences.zh: 」檜、俊不能屈，俊劫貴以私事，貴懼而從。

translations.literal: Qin Hui and Zhang Jun could not break him. Jun extorted Gui over a private matter, and Gui, in fear, complied.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui and Zhang Jun could not break him. Zhang Jun extorted Wang Gui over a private matter, and Wang Gui, in fear, complied.

sentences.zh: 時又有王俊者，善告訐，號「雕兒」，以奸貪屢為憲所裁。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a Wang Jun, skilled at informing, nicknamed the Eagle. Because of his corrupt greed he had repeatedly been punished by Xian.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was also a Wang Jun, skilled at informing, nicknamed the Eagle. Because of his corrupt greed he had repeatedly been punished by Zhang Xian.

sentences.zh: 檜使人諭之，俊輒從。

translations.literal: Qin Hui sent men to persuade him, and Jun readily complied.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui sent men to persuade him, and Wang Jun readily complied.

sentences.zh: 檜、俊謀以憲、貴、俊皆飛將，使其徒自相攻發，因及飛父子，庶主上不疑。

translations.literal: Qin Hui and Zhang Jun plotted that since Xian, Gui, and Jun were all Yue Fei's generals, they would have his own men attack one another in their accusations, thus implicating Yue Fei and his son, so that the emperor would not be suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui and Zhang Jun plotted that since Zhang Xian, Wang Gui, and Wang Jun were all Yue Fei's generals, they would have his own men attack one another in their accusations, thus implicating Yue Fei and his son, so that the emperor would not be suspicious.

sentences.zh: 俊自為狀付王俊，妄言憲謀還飛兵，令告王貴，使貴執憲。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun personally drew up a written statement and gave it to Wang Jun, falsely claiming that Xian plotted to restore Yue Fei's troops. He ordered Jun to inform Wang Gui and have Gui arrest Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun personally drew up a written statement and gave it to Wang Jun, falsely claiming that Zhang Xian plotted to restore Yue Fei's troops. He ordered Wang Jun to inform Wang Gui and have Wang Gui arrest Zhang Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲未至，俊預為獄以待之。

translations.literal: Before Xian even arrived, Jun had already prepared a prison to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhang Xian even arrived, Wang Jun had already prepared a prison to await him.

sentences.zh: 屬吏王應求白張俊，以為密院無推勘法。

translations.literal: A subordinate official Wang Yingqiu reported to Zhang Jun that the Privy Council had no authority to conduct interrogations.
translations.idiomatic: A subordinate official Wang Yingqiu reported to Zhang Jun that the Privy Council had no authority to conduct interrogations.

sentences.zh: 俊不聽，親行鞫煉，使憲自誣，謂得雲書，命憲營還兵計。

translations.literal: Jun would not listen. He personally conducted the torture-interrogation, forcing Xian to confess falsely, claiming he had received a letter from Yun and ordering Xian to draw up plans to restore the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun would not listen. He personally conducted the torture-interrogation, forcing Zhang Xian to confess falsely, claiming he had received a letter from Yue Yun and ordering Zhang Xian to draw up plans to restore the troops.

sentences.zh: 憲被掠無全膚，竟不伏。

translations.literal: Xian was tortured until not a patch of intact skin remained, yet in the end he would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian was tortured until not a patch of intact skin remained, yet in the end he would not confess.

sentences.zh: 俊手自具獄成，告檜械憲至行在，下大理寺。

translations.literal: Jun personally completed the case record and reported to Qin Hui, who had Xian shackled and brought to the temporary capital, where he was handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun personally completed the case record and reported to Qin Hui, who had Zhang Xian shackled and brought to the temporary capital, where he was handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 檜奏召飛父子證憲事。

translations.literal: Qin Hui memorialized requesting that Yue Fei and his son be summoned to testify in Xian's case.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui memorialized requesting that Yue Fei and his son be summoned to testify in Zhang Xian's case.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「刑所以止亂，勿妄追證，動搖人心。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Punishment exists to halt disorder. Do not recklessly pursue further testimony and shake people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Punishment exists to halt disorder. Do not recklessly pursue further testimony and shake people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」檜矯詔召飛父子至。

translations.literal: Qin Hui forged an edict summoning Yue Fei and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui forged an edict summoning Yue Fei and his son.

sentences.zh: 万俟禼誣飛使于鵬、孫革致書憲、貴，令虛申警報以動朝廷，雲與憲書規還飛軍。

translations.literal: Wan Qixie falsely charged that Yue Fei had sent Yu Peng and Sun Ge to write letters to Xian and Gui, ordering them to file false alarm reports to stir up the court, and that Yun had written to Xian planning to restore Yue Fei's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Qixie falsely charged that Yue Fei had sent Yu Peng and Sun Ge to write letters to Zhang Xian and Wang Gui, ordering them to file false alarm reports to stir up the court, and that Yue Yun had written to Zhang Xian planning to restore Yue Fei's army.

sentences.zh: 其書皆無有，乃妄稱憲、貴已焚之矣，但以眾證具獄。

translations.literal: None of these letters existed. They falsely claimed Xian and Gui had already burned them, and relied solely on collective testimony to complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: None of these letters existed. They falsely claimed Zhang Xian and Wang Gui had already burned them, and relied solely on collective testimony to complete the case.

sentences.zh: 語在飛《傳》。

translations.literal: The full account is in Yue Fei's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in Yue Fei's biography.

sentences.zh: 憲坐死，籍家貲。

translations.literal: Xian was executed and his family assets confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian was executed and his family assets confiscated.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十二年，追復龍神衛四廂都指揮使、閬州觀察使，贈寧遠軍承宣使，錄其家。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, his titles of commander of the fourth company of the Dragon Divine Guard and observation commissioner of Langzhou were posthumously restored. He was posthumously awarded the title of grand master for splendid remote service of Ningyuan Army, and his family was enrolled for office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, his titles of commander of the fourth company of the Dragon Divine Guard and observation commissioner of Langzhou were posthumously restored. He was posthumously awarded the title of grand master for splendid remote service of Ningyuan Army, and his family was enrolled for office.

sentences.zh: 楊再興

translations.literal: Yang Zaixing
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing

sentences.zh: 楊再興，賊曹成將也。

translations.literal: Yang Zaixing was a general under the bandit Cao Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing was a general under the bandit Cao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，岳飛破成，入莫邪關。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, Yue Fei defeated Cheng and entered Moyé Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing, Yue Fei defeated Cao Cheng and entered Moyé Pass.

sentences.zh: 第五將韓順夫解鞍脫甲，以所虜婦人佐酒。

translations.literal: The fifth company's Han Shunfu removed his saddle and armor, using captive women to help him drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth company's Han Shunfu removed his saddle and armor, using captive women to help him drink wine.

sentences.zh: 再興率眾直入其營，官軍卻，殺順夫，又殺飛弟飜。

translations.literal: Zaixing led his band straight into the camp. The government troops fell back. He killed Shunfu and also killed Yue Fei's younger brother Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing led his band straight into the camp. The government troops fell back. He killed Han Shunfu and also killed Yue Fei's younger brother Fan.

sentences.zh: 成敗，再興走躍入澗，張憲欲殺之，再興曰：「願執我見岳公。

translations.literal: Cheng was defeated. Zaixing leaped into a ravine to flee. Zhang Xian wished to kill him. Zaixing said: "I wish to be bound and brought before Lord Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cheng was defeated. Yang Zaixing leaped into a ravine to flee. Zhang Xian wished to kill him. Yang Zaixing said, "I wish to be bound and brought before Lord Yue.

sentences.zh: 」遂受縛。

translations.literal: He then submitted to being bound.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted to being bound.

sentences.zh: 飛見再興，奇其貌，釋之，曰：「吾不汝殺，汝當以忠義報國。

translations.literal: Yue Fei saw Zaixing, marveled at his appearance, and released him, saying: "I will not kill you. You should repay the state with loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei saw Yang Zaixing, marveled at his appearance, and released him, saying, "I will not kill you. You should repay the state with loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 」再興拜謝。

translations.literal: Zaixing bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 飛屯襄陽以圖中原，遣再興至西京長水縣之業陽，殺孫都統及統制滿在，斬五百餘人，俘將吏百人，餘黨奔潰。

translations.literal: Yue Fei encamped at Xiangyang planning to recover the Central Plain. He sent Zaixing to Yeyang in Changshui county of the Western Capital. Zaixing killed Supervisor Sun and controller Man Zai, beheaded more than five hundred men, captured one hundred officers and officials, and the rest fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei encamped at Xiangyang planning to recover the Central Plain. He sent Yang Zaixing to Yeyang in Changshui county of the Western Capital. Yang Zaixing killed Supervisor Sun and controller Man Zai, beheaded more than five hundred men, captured one hundred officers and officials, and the rest fled in collapse.

sentences.zh: 明日，再戰于孫洪澗，破其眾二千，復長水，得糧二萬石以給軍民，盡復西京險要。

translations.literal: The next day he fought again at Sunhong Stream, defeated two thousand of the enemy, recovered Changshui, obtained twenty thousand shi of grain to supply soldiers and civilians, and fully recovered the strategic points of the Western Capital region.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fought again at Sunhong Stream, defeated two thousand of the enemy, recovered Changshui, obtained twenty thousand shi of grain to supply soldiers and civilians, and fully recovered the strategic points of the Western Capital region.

sentences.zh: 又得偽齊所留馬萬匹，芻粟數十萬。

translations.literal: He also obtained ten thousand horses left behind by the puppet Qi regime and several hundred thousand units of fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He also obtained ten thousand horses left behind by the puppet Qi regime and several hundred thousand units of fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 中原回應。

translations.literal: The Central Plain responded in kind.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain responded in kind.

sentences.zh: 復至蔡州，焚賊糧。

translations.literal: He returned to Caizhou and burned the bandits' grain stores.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Caizhou and burned the bandits' grain stores.

sentences.zh: 飛敗金人於郾城，兀朮怒，合龍虎大王、蓋天大王及韓常兵逼之。

translations.literal: Yue Fei defeated the Jin at Yancheng. Wuzhu was enraged and combined the forces of the Dragon-Tiger King, the Sky-Covering King, and Han Chang to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei defeated the Jin at Yancheng. Wuzhu was enraged and combined the forces of the Dragon-Tiger King, the Sky-Covering King, and Han Chang to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 飛遣子雲當敵，鏖戰數十合，敵不支。

translations.literal: Yue Fei sent his son Yun to meet the enemy. They fought fiercely for several dozen engagements until the enemy could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei sent his son Yun to meet the enemy. They fought fiercely for several dozen engagements until the enemy could not hold.

sentences.zh: 再興以單騎入其軍，擒兀朮不獲，手殺數百人而還。

translations.literal: Zaixing rode alone into their army. He failed to capture Wuzhu but personally killed several hundred men and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing rode alone into their army. He failed to capture Wuzhu but personally killed several hundred men and returned.

sentences.zh: 兀朮憤甚，並力復來，頓兵十二萬於臨潁。

translations.literal: Wuzhu was greatly enraged. Massing his forces again, he stationed one hundred twenty thousand troops at Linying.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu was greatly enraged. Massing his forces again, he stationed one hundred twenty thousand troops at Linying.

sentences.zh: 再興以三百騎遇敵于小商橋，驟與之戰，殺二千餘人，及萬戶撒八孛堇、千戶百人。

translations.literal: Zaixing with three hundred cavalry encountered the enemy at Xiaoshang Bridge. He suddenly joined battle, killing more than two thousand men as well as the commander of ten thousand households Sabac, a military commander, and one hundred commanders of thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing with three hundred cavalry encountered the enemy at Xiaoshang Bridge. He suddenly joined battle, killing more than two thousand men as well as the commander of ten thousand households Sabac, a military commander, and one hundred commanders of thousand households.

sentences.zh: 再興戰死，後獲其屍，焚之，得箭鏃二升。

translations.literal: Zaixing died in battle. Later his body was recovered and cremated. Two sheng of arrowheads were found in it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaixing died in battle. Later his body was recovered and cremated. Two sheng of arrowheads were found in it.

sentences.zh: 牛皋，字伯遠，汝州魯山人。

translations.literal: Niu Gao, courtesy name Boyuan, was a native of Lushan in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Gao, courtesy name Boyuan, was a native of Lushan in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為射士，金人入侵，皋聚眾與戰，屢勝，西道總管翟興表補保義郎。

translations.literal: At first he was an archer. When the Jin invaded, Gao gathered a band to fight them and won repeatedly. Western Route commander Zhai Xing memorialized the throne recommending him for appointment as Gentleman of Protective Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was an archer. When the Jin invaded, Niu Gao gathered a band to fight them and won repeatedly. Western Route commander Zhai Xing memorialized the throne recommending him for appointment as Gentleman of Protective Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 杜充留守東京，皋討劇賊楊進于魯山，三戰三捷，賊黨奔潰。

translations.literal: When Du Chong held the eastern capital, Gao campaigned against the fierce bandit Yang Jin at Lushan. Three battles, three victories—the bandit followers fled in collapse.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chong held the eastern capital, Niu Gao campaigned against the fierce bandit Yang Jin at Lushan. Three battles, three victories—the bandit followers fled in collapse.

sentences.zh: 累遷榮州刺史、中軍統領。

translations.literal: He was promoted cumulatively to prefect of Rongzhou and commander of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted cumulatively to prefect of Rongzhou and commander of the central army.

sentences.zh: 金人再攻京西，皋十余戰皆捷。

translations.literal: When the Jin again attacked western Jing, Gao fought more than ten engagements, all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin again attacked western Jing, Niu Gao fought more than ten engagements, all victorious.

sentences.zh: 加果州團練使。

translations.literal: He was additionally made military training commissioner of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made military training commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 京城留守上官悟辟為同統制兼京西南路提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Capital garrison commander Shangguan Wu appointed him co-commander, concurrently serving as judicial intendant for southwestern Jing Road.
translations.idiomatic: Capital garrison commander Shangguan Wu appointed him co-commander, concurrently serving as judicial intendant for southwestern Jing Road.

sentences.zh: 金人攻江西者，自荊門北歸，皋潛軍于寶豐之宋村，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Jin troops who had attacked Jiangxi were returning north from Jingmen. Gao hid his army at Song village in Baofeng and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops who had attacked Jiangxi were returning north from Jingmen. Niu Gao hid his army at Song village in Baofeng and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 轉和州防禦使，充五軍都統制。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defender-in-chief of Hezhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defender-in-chief of Hezhou and appointed commander-in-chief of the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 又與孛堇戰魯山鄧家橋，敗之。

translations.literal: He also fought a military commander at Deng Family Bridge in Lushan and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought a Jin military commander at Deng Family Bridge in Lushan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 轉西道招撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Western Route.

sentences.zh: 偽齊乞師于金入寇，皋設伏要地，自屯丹霞以待。

translations.literal: The puppet Qi regime requested Jin troops to join an invasion. Gao set ambushes at key points and personally encamped at Danxia to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet Qi regime requested Jin troops to join an invasion. Niu Gao set ambushes at key points and personally encamped at Danxia to await them.

sentences.zh: 敵兵悉眾來，伏發，俘其酋豪鄭務兒。

translations.literal: The enemy came with their full strength. The ambush was sprung, and their chieftain Zheng Wu'er was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came with their full strength. The ambush was sprung, and their chieftain Zheng Wu'er was captured.

sentences.zh: 遷安州觀察使，尋除蔡唐州信陽軍鎮撫使、知蔡州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Anzhou. Soon he was removed from that post and made pacification commissioner of Caizhou, Tangzhou, and Xinyang Army, and prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Anzhou. Soon he was removed from that post and made pacification commissioner of Caizhou, Tangzhou, and Xinyang Army, and prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 遇敵戰輒勝，加親衛大夫。

translations.literal: Whenever he met the enemy in battle he won. He was additionally made Defender-in-Chief of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met the enemy in battle he won. He was additionally made Defender-in-Chief of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 會岳飛制置江西、湖北，將由襄、漢規中原，命皋隸飛軍。

translations.literal: When Yue Fei was appointed to oversee Jiangxi and Hubei, planning to advance on the Central Plain via Xiang and Han, Gao was ordered to serve under Yue Fei's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei was appointed to oversee Jiangxi and Hubei, planning to advance on the Central Plain via Xiang and Han, Niu Gao was ordered to serve under Yue Fei's command.

sentences.zh: 飛喜甚，即辟為唐鄧襄郢州安撫使，尋改神武后軍中部統領。

translations.literal: Yue Fei was greatly pleased and immediately appointed him pacification commissioner of Tang, Deng, Xiang, and Ying prefectures. Soon he was changed to commander of the middle section of the Shenwu Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was greatly pleased and immediately appointed him pacification commissioner of Tang, Deng, Xiang, and Ying prefectures. Soon he was changed to commander of the middle section of the Shenwu Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 偽齊使李成合金人入寇，破襄陽六郡。

translations.literal: The puppet Qi regime sent Li Cheng to join Jin troops in an invasion, smashing the six prefectures of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet Qi regime sent Li Cheng to join Jin troops in an invasion, smashing the six prefectures of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 敵將王嵩在隨州，飛遣皋行，裹三日糧。

translations.literal: The enemy general Wang Song was at Suizhou. Yue Fei sent Gao on the mission with three days' rations.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Wang Song was at Suizhou. Yue Fei sent Niu Gao on the mission with three days' rations.

sentences.zh: 糧未盡，城已拔，執嵩斬之，得卒五千，遂復隨州。

translations.literal: Before the rations were exhausted the city had already been taken. He seized Song and executed him, obtained five thousand soldiers, and thus recovered Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rations were exhausted the city had already been taken. He seized Wang Song and executed him, obtained five thousand soldiers, and thus recovered Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 李成在襄陽，飛遣皋以騎兵擊破之，復襄陽。

translations.literal: Li Cheng was at Xiangyang. Yue Fei sent Gao with cavalry to smash him and recover Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was at Xiangyang. Yue Fei sent Niu Gao with cavalry to smash him and recover Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 金人攻淮西，飛遣皋渡江，自提兵與皋會。

translations.literal: When the Jin attacked western Huai, Yue Fei sent Gao across the river; he personally led troops to join Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked western Huai, Yue Fei sent Niu Gao across the river; he personally led troops to join Niu Gao.

sentences.zh: 時偽齊驅甲騎五千薄廬州，皋遙謂金將曰：「牛皋在此，爾輩胡為見犯？

translations.literal: At that time the puppet Qi drove five thousand armored cavalry to press close to Luzhou. Gao shouted from afar to the Jin general: "Niu Gao is here—why do you dare intrude upon us?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the puppet Qi drove five thousand armored cavalry to press close to Luzhou. Niu Gao shouted from afar to the Jin general, "Niu Gao is here—why do you dare intrude upon us?

sentences.zh: 」眾皆愕然，不戰而潰。

translations.literal: All were astonished and fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy troops were thunderstruck and broke ranks without even putting up a fight.

sentences.zh: 飛謂皋曰：「必追之，去而復來，無益也。

translations.literal: Yue Fei said to Gao: "You must pursue them—if they go away and come back, it will do no good."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei told Niu Gao, "You must pursue them. If they withdraw only to return, it will do no good."

sentences.zh: 」皋追擊三十余里，金人相踐及殺死者相半，斬其副都統及千戶五人，百戶數十人，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Gao pursued for over thirty li. The Jin trampled one another, and those killed were half their number. He cut down their deputy commander-in-chief and five commanders of thousand-household units, and several dozen commanders of hundred-household units. The army's reputation rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Gao pursued for more than thirty li. Half the Jin force was killed or trampled in the rout; he cut down their deputy commander-in-chief, five thousand-household commanders, and several dozen hundred-household commanders. The army's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 廬州平，進中侍大夫。

translations.literal: Luzhou was pacified; he was promoted to Palace Attendant Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: With Luzhou pacified, he was promoted to Palace Attendant Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 從平楊麼，破之。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Yang Mo and smashed him.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign to suppress Yang Mo and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 麼技窮，舉鐘子儀投于水，繼乃自僕。

translations.literal: Mo's stratagems were exhausted; he lifted Zhong Ziyi and threw him into the water, then forthwith threw himself down.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mo was out of options. He seized Zhong Ziyi and threw him into the water, then immediately fell on his face in surrender.

sentences.zh: 皋投水擒麼，飛斬首函送都督行府。

translations.literal: Gao plunged into the water and captured Mo. Yue Fei cut off his head, put it in a box, and sent it to the commander's field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Gao leapt into the water and captured Yang Mo. Yue Fei cut off his head, boxed it, and sent it to the commander's field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 除武泰軍承宣使，改行營護聖中軍統制，尋充湖北、京西宣撫司左軍統制，加龍、神衛四廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Promotion Commissioner of the Wutai Army, then changed to commander of the middle army of the Mobile Camp Guard of the Sacred Presence; shortly thereafter he served as commander of the left army of the Hubei and Jingxi Pacification Commission, and was additionally made commander of all four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Promotion Commissioner of the Wutai Army, then reassigned as commander of the middle army of the Mobile Camp Guard of the Sacred Presence; soon after he became commander of the left wing of the Hubei–Jingxi Pacification Commission and was additionally promoted to commander of all four wings of the Dragon and Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 金人渝盟，飛命皋出師戰汴、許間，以功最，除捧日天武四廂都指揮使、成德軍承宣使，樞密行府以皋兼提舉一行事務。

translations.literal: When the Jin broke the treaty, Yue Fei ordered Gao to take the field and fight between Bian and Xu. For the highest merit he was appointed commander of all four wings of the Sun-Bearing Heavenly Martial Guard and Military Promotion Commissioner of the Chengde Army; the Mobile Privy Council headquarters had Gao additionally oversee all its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the peace, Yue Fei ordered Niu Gao to take the field between Bian and Xu. For outstanding service he was made commander of all four wings of the Sun-Bearing Heavenly Martial Guard and Military Promotion Commissioner of the Chengde Army; the mobile Privy Council headquarters put him in charge of all its affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 宣撫司罷，改鄂州駐劄御前左軍統制，升真定府路馬步軍副統總管，轉甯國軍承宣使、荊湖南路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: When the Pacification Commission was abolished, he was made commander of the left army of the Imperial Guard stationed at Ezhou, promoted to deputy overall commander of the mounted and foot forces of the Zhending Prefecture circuit, and transferred to Military Promotion Commissioner of the Ningguo Army and deputy overall commander of the mounted and foot forces of the Jinghu South circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pacification Commission was dissolved, he was reassigned as commander of the left wing of the Imperial Guard at Ezhou, promoted to deputy overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Zhending circuit, and made Military Promotion Commissioner of the Ningguo Army and deputy overall commander of cavalry and infantry in southern Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 紹興十七年上巳日，都統制田師中大會諸將，皋遇毒，亟歸，語所親曰：「皋年六十一，官至侍從，幸不啻足。

translations.literal: On the Upper Si day in the seventeenth year of Shaoxing, overall commander Tian Shizhong held a great assembly of the generals. Gao encountered poison, hurried home, and said to those close to him: "Gao is sixty-one years old, his office has reached attendant-in-waiting rank—fortunately, that is more than enough."
translations.idiomatic: On the Upper Si festival day in the seventeenth year of Shaoxing, overall commander Tian Shizhong held a grand gathering of the generals. Niu Gao was poisoned, hurried home, and told his intimates, "I am sixty-one years old and have reached attendant-in-waiting rank—surely that is more than enough."

sentences.zh: 所恨南北通和，不以馬革裹屍，顧死牖下耳。

translations.literal: What I regret is that north and south are at peace—I shall not die with my corpse wrapped in horsehide, but only die beneath my window."
translations.idiomatic: My regret is that with north and south at peace, I shall not die on the battlefield with my body wrapped in horsehide, but only perish beneath my own roof."

sentences.zh: 」明日卒。

translations.literal: The next day he died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he died.

sentences.zh: 或言秦檜使師中毒皋雲。

translations.literal: Some say Qin Hui had Shizhong poison Gao, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some held that Qin Hui had Tian Shizhong poison Niu Gao.

sentences.zh: 初，檜主和，未幾，金渝盟入侵，帝手劄賜飛從便措置。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qin had advocated peace. Before long the Jin broke the treaty and invaded. The emperor sent a hand-written edict granting Yue Fei discretion in arranging matters as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: At first Qin Hui had pressed for peace. Before long the Jin broke the treaty and invaded. The emperor sent Yue Fei a personally written edict granting him full discretion.

sentences.zh: 飛乃命皋及王貴、董先、楊再興、孟邦傑、李寶等經略東西京、汝、鄭、潁、陳、曹、光、蔡諸郡；

translations.literal: Yue Fei then ordered Gao, Wang Gui, Dong Xian, Yang Zaixing, Meng Bangjie, Li Bao, and others to manage the prefectures of the Eastern and Western Capitals, Ru, Zheng, Ying, Chen, Cao, Guang, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei then ordered Niu Gao, Wang Gui, Dong Xian, Yang Zaixing, Meng Bangjie, Li Bao, and others to secure the Eastern and Western Capitals and the prefectures of Ru, Zheng, Ying, Chen, Cao, Guang, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 又遣梁興渡河，糾合忠義社取河東北州縣。

translations.literal: He also sent Liang Xing across the river to rally the Loyal and Righteous Societies and seize the prefectures and counties of northeast Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Liang Xing across the river to rally the Loyal and Righteous Societies and take the prefectures and counties of northeastern Hedong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李寶捷于曹州，捷于宛亭，捷於渤海廟；

translations.literal: Before long Li Bao scored victories at Caozhou, at Wanting, and at Bohai Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Bao won victories at Caozhou, at Wanting, and at Bohai Temple.

sentences.zh: 董先、姚政捷於潁昌；

translations.literal: Dong Xian and Yao Zheng scored victories at Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian and Yao Zheng won victories at Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 劉政捷于中牟。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng scored a victory at Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng won a victory at Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 張憲復潁昌、淮寧府；

translations.literal: Zhang Xian recovered Yingchang and Huaining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian recovered Yingchang and Huaining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王貴之將楊成復鄭州；

translations.literal: Wang Gui's officer Yang Cheng recovered Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Cheng, an officer under Wang Gui, recovered Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 張應、韓清復西京。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying and Han Qing recovered the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying and Han Qing recovered the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 皋及傅選捷於京西，捷于黃河上。

translations.literal: Gao and Fu Xuan scored victories in western Jing and on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Gao and Fu Xuan won victories in western Jing and along the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 孟邦傑復永安軍，其將楊遇復南城軍，又與劉政捷於西京。

translations.literal: Meng Bangjie recovered Yong'an Army; his officer Yang Yu recovered Nancheng Army; he also joined Liu Zheng in a victory at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Bangjie recovered Yong'an Army; his officer Yang Yu recovered Nancheng Army; Meng also fought alongside Liu Zheng to victory at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 梁興會太行忠義及兩河豪傑趙雲、李進、董榮、牛顯、張峪等破金人于垣曲，又捷于沁水，追至孟州之邵原，金張太保、成太保等以所部降，又破金高太尉兵于濟源。

translations.literal: Liang Xing joined the loyalists of the Taihang and the heroes of the two He regions—Zhao Yun, Li Jin, Dong Rong, Niu Xian, Zhang Yu, and others—and defeated the Jin at Yuanqu. He scored another victory at Qinshui, pursued to Shaoyuan in Mengzhou; Jin commanders Zhang the Grand Tutor, Cheng the Grand Tutor, and others surrendered with their forces; he also defeated the Jin troops of Senior Captain Gao at Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xing joined Taihang loyalists and heroes from the two He regions—Zhao Yun, Li Jin, Dong Rong, Niu Xian, Zhang Yu, and others—to defeat the Jin at Yuanqu. He won again at Qinshui and pursued the enemy to Shaoyuan in Mengzhou, where Jin commanders Zhang the Grand Tutor, Cheng the Grand Tutor, and others surrendered with their troops; he also routed the Jin forces of Senior Captain Gao at Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 喬握堅等復趙州；

translations.literal: Qiao Wojian and others recovered Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Wojian and his fellows recovered Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李興捷于河南府，捷于永安軍；

translations.literal: Li Xing scored victories at Henan Prefecture and at Yong'an Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xing won victories at Henan Prefecture and at Yong'an Army.

sentences.zh: 梁興在河北取懷、衛二州，大破兀朮軍，斷山東、河北金帛馬綱之路，金人大擾。

translations.literal: Liang Xing, in Hebei, took the two prefectures of Huai and Wei, heavily defeated Wuzhu's army, and cut the route by which gold, silk, and horses were transported from Shandong and Hebei; the Jin were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei, Liang Xing captured Huai and Wei, routed Wuzhu's army, and severed the Jin supply routes for gold, silk, and horses from Shandong and Hebei, throwing the enemy into great turmoil.

sentences.zh: 未幾，岳飛還朝，下獄死，世以為恨雲。

translations.literal: Before long Yue Fei returned to court, was imprisoned and died; the world considered it a cause for regret, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yue Fei was recalled to court, thrown into prison, and died—a loss the age deeply mourned.

sentences.zh: 胡閎休

translations.literal: Hu Hongxiu
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hongxiu

sentences.zh: 胡閎休，字良㢸，開封人。

translations.literal: Hu Hongxiu, courtesy name Liangbian, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Hongxiu, styled Liangbian, was a native of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，入太學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuanhe reign, he entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xuanhe era, he enrolled in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時方諱兵，閎休著《兵書》二卷。

translations.literal: At the time military matters were taboo; Hongxiu wrote two scrolls titled Military Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs were then a forbidden topic, but Hongxiu wrote a two-scroll Military Treatise.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，創知兵科，閎休應試，中優等，補承信郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, the Military Knowledge examination was newly established. Hongxiu took the test, placed in the highest grade, and was appointed Gentlemen for Manifest Trust.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang era a new examination in military knowledge was instituted. Hongxiu sat for it, earned top honors, and was appointed Gentlemen for Manifest Trust.

sentences.zh: 金人圍城，閎休分地而守。

translations.literal: When the Jin besieged the city, Hongxiu divided the ground and defended it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin besieged the capital, Hongxiu organized the defense by sector.

sentences.zh: 二帝詣金營，閎休欲結義士劫之，何㮚禁止之。
