translations.literal: When the two emperors went to the Jin camp, Hongxiu wished to gather loyal men to rescue them by force, but He Li forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When the two emperors were taken to the Jin camp, Hongxiu wanted to rally loyal men to rescue them by force, but He Li forbade it.

sentences.zh: 二帝北遷，範瓊散勤王師，閎休曰：「勤王師可進不可退。

translations.literal: When the two emperors were moved north, Fan Qiong dispersed the armies that had marched to save the throne. Hongxiu said: "Armies that march to save the throne may advance but must not retreat."
translations.idiomatic: After the two emperors were carried north, Fan Qiong disbanded the relief armies. Hongxiu said, "Armies raised to save the throne may advance but must never retreat."

sentences.zh: 」檄令隨軍而無靖康年號，閎休得之泣下，懷檄而走，從辛道宗勤王。

translations.literal: A proclamation accompanied the army but bore no Jingkang reign title. When Hongxiu received it he wept, clutched the proclamation, and fled to join Xin Daozong's army marching to save the throne.
translations.idiomatic: A military proclamation circulated with the troops but carried no Jingkang reign title. Hongxiu wept when he saw it, tucked the document inside his robe, and fled to join Xin Daozong's relief force.

sentences.zh: 南渡，以忠義進兩官。

translations.literal: After crossing south, he was promoted two ranks for loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south, he was promoted two ranks in recognition of his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 湖湘盜起，或曰招之便，或曰討之便，閎休作《致寇》、《禦寇》二篇，言天地之氣，先春後秋，招之不伏則討之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Hunan and Hubei, some said it would be expedient to summon them, others said it would be expedient to suppress them. Hongxiu wrote two essays, "Inviting Bandits" and "Defending against Bandits," stating that the qi of Heaven and Earth comes first in spring and later in autumn—that if summoning them did not make them submit, then they should be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Hunan and Hubei, some argued for summoning them to surrender and others for crushing them by force. Hongxiu wrote two essays, Inviting Banditry and Repelling Banditry, arguing that Heaven's seasonal rhythm runs from spring to autumn: summon first, and suppress only if they refuse to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是以岳飛為招討使，飛辟閎休為主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue Fei was made Pacification Commissioner; Yue Fei recruited Hongxiu as chief draftsman for strategic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was accordingly appointed Pacification Commissioner, and he recruited Hongxiu as his chief adviser on military plans.

sentences.zh: 以誅鐘子儀功，進成忠郎。

translations.literal: For his merit in executing Zhong Ziyi, he was promoted to Attendant for Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in the execution of Zhong Ziyi, he was promoted to Attendant for Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 飛被誣死，閎休發憤杜門，佯疾十年，卒。

translations.literal: When Yue Fei was falsely accused and died, Hongxiu, burning with indignation, shut his doors, feigned illness for ten years, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue Fei died under false accusation, Hongxiu shut himself away in bitter rage, feigned illness for ten years, and then died.

sentences.zh: 有《勤王忠義集》藏於家。

translations.literal: He had a collection titled Gatherings of Loyalty in Saving the Throne, kept in his home.
translations.idiomatic: His writings were collected in Loyalty in Saving the Throne, kept in his family.

sentences.zh: 孫照，德安太守。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhao was prefect of De'an.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhao served as prefect of De'an.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王德素有威略，蚤隸劉光世，審其不可恃；

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wang De had always possessed martial authority and stratagem. He early served under Liu Guangshi and discerned that Liu could not be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Wang De had long possessed both authority and strategic insight. He served Liu Guangshi early on and saw clearly that Liu was not a man to rely on.

sentences.zh: 晚從張俊，竟以功名顯，其知所擇哉。

translations.literal: Late in life he followed Zhang Jun and finally achieved fame through merit and office—is this not knowing whom to choose?
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he follow Zhang Jun, and in the end he won fame and rank through merit—surely he knew how to choose his master.

sentences.zh: 王彥棄家赴國，累破堅敵，威振河朔；

translations.literal: Wang Yan abandoned his family to serve the state, repeatedly smashed stubborn foes, and his awe shook Heshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan left his home to serve the dynasty, broke stubborn enemies again and again, and his renown shook the northern Yellow River region.

sentences.zh: 晚奪兵柄，使之治郡，用違其材，惜矣。

translations.literal: Late in life his command was taken from him and he was made to govern a prefecture—the use fell short of his talent; how regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years his command was stripped away and he was sent to govern a prefecture—a waste of his abilities, and a pity.

sentences.zh: 魏勝崛起，無甲兵糧餉之資，提數千烏合之眾，抗金人數十萬之師，卒完一州，名震當時，壯哉！

translations.literal: Wei Sheng rose suddenly, without resources of armor, weapons, or provisions; he led several thousand men gathered in disorder to resist several hundred thousand Jin troops, finally preserved one prefecture, and his name shook the age—how heroic!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng rose from nothing, without arms, armor, or supply lines, yet led a few thousand raw recruits against Jin armies numbering in the hundreds of thousands, held a prefecture intact, and made a name that shook his age—magnificent!

sentences.zh: 然見忌于諸將，無援而戰死，亦可惜矣。

translations.literal: Yet he was envied by the generals, fought with no relief, and died in battle—also regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the other generals envied him; cut off from help, he died in battle—a loss to be mourned indeed.

sentences.zh: 張憲等五人皆岳飛部將，為敵所畏，亦一時之傑也；

translations.literal: Zhang Xian and the other four were all officers under Yue Fei, feared by the enemy—they too were heroes of their age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xian and the four others were all Yue Fei's officers, and the enemy feared them—they were heroes of their day as well.

sentences.zh: 然或以戰沒，或以憤卒，而憲以不證飛獄冤死，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yet some died in battle, some died of indignant grief, while Xian, for refusing to testify against Yue Fei in the prison case, died unjustly—how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: Some fell in battle, others died of righteous fury—but Zhang Xian died wrongfully because he would not testify against Yue Fei in the prison interrogation. How tragic!
